Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Part C data call calendar for every MA contract (H-number); escalation to the Head of Compliance when a CMS window is at risk

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 42 CFR 422.310 (risk adjustment data), 422.137/422.138 and 422.101(b), re-read against the current e-CFR text and the CMS Risk Adjustment Data Submission and Processing Technical Specifications each contract year

In-scope processes.value: Annual risk adjustment data call intake: HPMS memo monitoring, EDS/RAPS submission-window scheduling, sweep-date back-scheduling and CMS model-run deadline tracking for every H-number and PBP

In-scope systems.value: CMS HPMS memo feed and the Part C data call calendar; encounter source data staged in the enterprise data warehouse before EDFES submission

Compliance procedure documented.value: Part C Risk Adjustment Data Call Calendar Procedure - HPMS memo triage, deadline derivation from the CMS technical specifications, back-scheduled internal cut dates, owner assignment per H-number

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Medicare Compliance Officer and refreshed each contract year when CMS publishes the updated Risk Adjustment Data Submission technical specifications

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: CMS initial and final risk adjustment model-run submission deadlines for the payment year (the CMS-announced first-Monday-in-September initial sweep and the final reconciliation sweep), plus the 13-months-from-date-of-service internal encounter submission cut

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar alerts at T-90, T-45, T-14 and T-3 days before each CMS sweep date, addressed to the named H-number owner and the Regulatory Reporting Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Data call calendar versions, HPMS memo captures and sweep-date derivations retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d) in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed or unregistered CMS sweep window is logged as a Part C reporting exception with H-number, dates of service affected and payment impact

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Medicare Compliance Officer signs off every missed sweep window and the associated late-submission recovery plan

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every CMS Part C risk adjustment submission window and HPMS-announced data call applicable to the organization's H-numbers for the payment year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any applicable CMS data call absent from the calendar, or any sweep date recorded later than the CMS-published date, is a fail; one fail escalates to the Medicare Compliance Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs annually per payment year with in-year sweeps; the test runs semi-annually, ahead of the September initial sweep and after the final reconciliation sweep

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not own any H-number on the data call calendar

Evidence location for test results.value: Part C data call calendar completeness workpaper (HPMS memo sweep, calendar extract, deadline re-derivation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar export by H-number with CMS sweep dates, submission receipts and HPMS memo references, producible for a CMS program audit within the 3-business-day universe request window

Regulator response path.value: The Medicare Compliance Officer is the single point of contact for the CMS Account Manager; all HPMS responses are cleared by Regulatory Counsel before submission

checklist.step: Open the payment-year Part C data call calendar for every contract
actions: Pull the current list of active MA contracts (H-numbers) and PBPs from the Medicare Compliance Officer and enter one calendar section per H-number.

Create a calendar row for each recurring CMS risk adjustment obligation: EDS encounter submission windows, the initial model-run sweep, the mid-year sweep and the final reconciliation sweep for the payment year.
On each row record: obligation name, citation (42 CFR 422.310), CMS sweep date, dates of service covered, submitting entity, named owner and backup owner.
Set the calendar version to <payment year>-v1 and circulate it to Data Management, the Encounter Data lead and Actuarial for confirmation of ownership.
checklist.done: every active H-number has a dated calendar section with a named owner and backup for each CMS risk adjustment window.

checklist.step: Sweep CMS HPMS memos weekly for new or changed data calls
actions: Log in to CMS HPMS and open Home > HPMS Memos, filter Category = 'Risk Adjustment' and 'Plan Reporting' and Date = last 7 days.
Download every memo that names a submission window, sweep date, deadline change or new data request and save it as hpms-memo-<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.pdf.
For each memo write a one-line triage note: applies / does not apply, which H-numbers, which calendar row it changes.
Hand applicable memos to the Data Management encounter lead and the Actuarial Analyst who owns risk score projections, and log the handoff date.
Where the memo moves a date, bump the calendar version and record the old date, the new date and the memo reference on the row.
checklist.done: every HPMS memo issued in the week has a dated triage note and, where applicable, a versioned calendar change referencing the memo.

checklist.step: Derive each CMS deadline from the current technical specifications rather than last year's calendar
actions: Open the current CMS Risk Adjustment Data Submission and Processing technical specifications (Encounter Data Submission and Processing Guide) for the payment year.
Read the deadline table and copy, verbatim, the sentence that fixes each sweep date and the dates of service it covers onto the calendar row.
Confirm the initial model-run submission deadline (the CMS-announced first Monday in September following the payment year) and the final reconciliation deadline as published, not as remembered.
Record the internal 13-months-from-date-of-service encounter submission cut alongside the CMS date so late claims are caught before the window closes.
Attach the specification page capture to the calendar row as the source of the date.
checklist.done: every calendar date carries a quoted source sentence and an attached page capture from the current-year CMS specifications.

checklist.step: Map each calendar row to its source system, data owner and extract job
actions: For each risk adjustment row name the source of record: the claims platform for professional and institutional encounters, the provider-submitted chart review feed, and the delegated-entity encounter files.
Record the warehouse schema and table that stages the encounter population, and the scheduled extract job id that feeds the EDFES submitter.
Name the accountable data steward for each source and confirm in writing that they accept the calendar dates.
Flag any row whose source is a vendor or delegated entity so contractual submission lead times can be added.
checklist.done: every calendar row names a source of record, a staging table, an extract job id and an accepting data steward.

checklist.step: Confirm submitter identifiers and EDFES connectivity before the first window
actions: Verify the organization's Submitter ID, contract H-number and EDFES/EDPS connection credentials are active with the CMS MAC/EDS front-end for the payment year.
Run a test 837 file through the EDFES and confirm the TA1, 999 and 277CA acknowledgements return without connectivity errors.
Record the round-trip time from submission to 277CA in the calendar row so the back-schedule reflects real processing lag.
Raise a ticket with the CMS EDI help desk for any credential or connectivity failure and log the ticket number against the affected windows.
checklist.done: a test file has cleared EDFES with acknowledgements returned, and the observed processing lag is recorded on each window row.

checklist.step: Back-schedule internal cut dates off every CMS sweep date
actions: For each window compute: data freeze date = CMS sweep date minus (EDFES processing lag + error-correction cycle + resubmission buffer).
Use a minimum 30-calendar-day resubmission buffer so a rejected file can be corrected and resubmitted inside the window.
Write freeze date, submission target date, error-resolution cut date and CMS sweep date onto the calendar row.
Publish the freeze dates to Data Management, the claims operations lead and the delegated-entity oversight manager so upstream feeds close in time.
checklist.done: every window shows a computed freeze date, submission target, error-resolution cut and CMS sweep date, published to the upstream owners.

checklist.step: Configure reminders and the escalation ladder on every row
actions: Set automated alerts at T-90, T-45, T-14 and T-3 days before each CMS sweep date to the row owner and backup.
Set a second alert at T-7 days before each internal freeze date to the Data Management steward who owns the extract.
Configure escalation so an unacknowledged T-14 alert routes to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and an unacknowledged T-3 alert routes to the Medicare Compliance Officer.
Send yourself a test alert on one row and confirm delivery before relying on the configuration.
checklist.done: each row has four dated reminders, a freeze-date reminder and a two-step escalation, with delivery proven by a test alert.

checklist.step: Extend the calendar to the Part C reporting-requirements data calls
actions: Open the current CMS Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications and list every reportable section that applies to the organization's contracts (organization determinations and reconsiderations, grievances, special needs plan care management, payments to providers, rewards and incentives).
Add one calendar row per section per H-number with its reporting period and its CMS-published due date from the specification's reporting deadline table.
Mark SNP-only sections as not applicable for non-SNP contracts and record the reason on the row so the omission is deliberate.
Cross-reference each row to 42 CFR 422.516 and to the responsible operational team (Appeals and Grievances, Care Management, Network).
checklist.done: every applicable 422.516 reporting section appears as its own dated calendar row, and every non-applicable section carries a written reason.

checklist.step: Capture delegated-entity and first-tier downstream submission obligations
actions: Pull the delegated-entity register (delegated risk groups, IPAs, PBM, vendor claims processors) from the vendor oversight team.
For each delegate confirm the contractual encounter and reporting submission dates in the delegation agreement and record them on the calendar as upstream feeder rows.
Set each delegate feeder date at least 15 calendar days ahead of the internal freeze date so late delegate files can still be processed.
Notify each delegate's relationship owner in writing of the payment-year dates and file the acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every delegate that supplies encounter or reporting data has a feeder date on the calendar and a filed acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Register the data-accuracy certification dependency for each submission
actions: For each CMS submission window add a certification row citing 42 CFR 422.504(l) - the CEO, CFO or delegate must certify the accuracy, completeness and truthfulness of the risk adjustment data.
Name the certifying officer and the delegate of record, and record the delegation document reference.
Set the certification due date at 5 business days before the CMS sweep date so a refusal to certify still leaves time to correct data.
Route a calendar invitation with the certification package deadline to the certifying officer.
checklist.done: every submission window has a named certifying officer, a delegation reference and a certification date ahead of the CMS sweep.

checklist.step: Review the calendar at the monthly Part C reporting governance forum
actions: Present the calendar filtered to rows due in the next 90 days, with RAG status per row.
Walk each amber and red row: what is blocking, who owns it, what the recovery date is.
Minute every date change agreed at the forum and republish the calendar version the same day.
Record attendance so the forum's oversight can be evidenced to CMS in a program audit.
checklist.done: minuted monthly forum record showing every 90-day row reviewed, with owners and recovery dates for amber and red rows.

checklist.step: Handle off-cycle CMS requests, RADV audits and ad hoc data calls
actions: On receipt of an HPMS notice of a RADV audit, program audit universe request or ad hoc data call, open a calendar row within one business day.

Copy the CMS-stated response window onto the row exactly as written (program audit universes are commonly due within 3 business days of the engagement letter; RADV medical record submission windows are stated in the HPMS notice).
Assign the row to the named universe owner, and book the daily stand-up cadence for the response period.
Notify Regulatory Counsel and the Medicare Compliance Officer the same day the notice arrives.
checklist.done: every off-cycle CMS request is on the calendar within one business day with the CMS-stated window, an owner and counsel notified.

checklist.step: Track submission status against the calendar weekly
actions: Each Monday update every open row with: file submitted Y/N, EDFES acknowledgement received Y/N, MAO-002 accepted/rejected counts, and percentage of the expected encounter population accepted.
Compare accepted encounter counts to the warehouse expected-volume baseline and flag any row below 98 percent acceptance.
Reforecast the row's completion date where acceptance is short and record the new date with the reason.
Send the weekly status to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Data Governance Lead.
checklist.done: every open row carries a current-week submission status, acceptance percentage and, where short, a reforecast date.

checklist.step: Escalate any window that can no longer be met
actions: Where the computed freeze date has passed without a complete data set, raise the escalation to the Medicare Compliance Officer and the Chief Financial Officer within one business day.
Present in writing the affected H-numbers, dates of service, estimated risk score and revenue impact, and the recovery options.
Decide and record the action: expedited extract, partial submission with a follow-up file inside the window, or a documented late submission with a CMS notification.
Log the decision, its owner and the notification date on the calendar row - allowing a window to lapse silently is never an option.
checklist.done: every at-risk window has a written, owned decision and, where applicable, a dated CMS notification.

checklist.step: Close and archive the payment-year calendar
actions: After the final reconciliation sweep, freeze the final calendar version and export it to PDF with the version history intact.
Bundle it with the HPMS memo captures, specification page captures, submission receipts and certification records for the payment year.
File the bundle under Medicare Advantage > Part C Reporting > <payment year> and apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the repository index makes the bundle searchable by H-number, payment year and sweep date.
checklist.done: the frozen payment-year calendar bundle is filed with a 10-year retention label and is searchable by H-number and sweep date.

testing.step: Build the independent population of CMS data calls for the payment year
actions: Pull every HPMS memo issued in the payment year under the Risk Adjustment and Plan Reporting categories directly from HPMS > Home > HPMS Memos - do not start from the compliance calendar.
Add every reportable section listed in the CMS Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications deadline table and every sweep date in the Encounter Data Submission and Processing Guide.
Filter to those applicable to the organization's active H-numbers using the CMS contract list, and record the applicability test used.
Sign the population as complete, stating the extraction date and the HPMS filters applied.
testing.done: a signed, independently sourced population of applicable data calls exists with the extraction filters documented.

testing.step: Reconcile the independent population to the compliance calendar
actions: Match each population item to a calendar row on obligation name + H-number + reporting period.
List calendar rows with no population match (potentially obsolete) and population items with no calendar row (missed obligations) separately.
For every unmatched population item, confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Manager whether it was tracked elsewhere and obtain the evidence, or record it as an exception.
Reconcile the counts and show the difference bridge in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the calendar with a documented bridge and every unmatched item resolved or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible sample
actions: Take 100 percent of risk adjustment sweep windows and 100 percent of RADV or program audit ad hoc rows.
Take 15 rows selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining 422.516 reporting rows, minimum 25 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn by a third party.
State in the workpaper why any stratum was excluded.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, stratified, reproducible from the recorded seed and covers every sweep window.

testing.step: Re-derive each sampled deadline from the CMS source
actions: For each sampled row open the CMS technical specification or HPMS memo yourself and read the deadline sentence before looking at the calendar row.
Record your own derived date, then compare it to the calendar date; a difference of any size is an exception, including a correct date supported by the wrong citation.
Confirm the dates of service covered by each sweep match the specification's stated service period.
Screenshot the specification page relied upon into the workpaper with its publication date.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independently derived date, a comparison result and a captured CMS source page.

testing.step: Trace sampled rows to a submission receipt and a CMS acknowledgement
actions: For each sampled risk adjustment row, obtain the EDFES submission confirmation, the 999 and 277CA acknowledgements and the MAO-002 report for the file.
Confirm the submission timestamp is on or before the CMS sweep date and that the file's contract H-number matches the row.
For 422.516 rows obtain the HPMS Plan Reporting Module submission confirmation screen showing status Submitted and the submission date.
Record any row with no retrievable receipt as an exception even where the team asserts the submission was made.
testing.done: every sampled row traces to a dated submission receipt and CMS acknowledgement that pre-dates the deadline.

testing.step: Recompute the back-schedule and reminder maths
actions: For 10 sampled rows recompute freeze date = CMS sweep date minus (observed EDFES lag + error-correction cycle + 30-day resubmission buffer).
Compare your recomputed freeze date to the recorded one and note any row where the recorded freeze date leaves less than the 30-day buffer.
Extract the reminder configuration and confirm alerts exist at T-90, T-45, T-14 and T-3 with the correct recipient.
Confirm from the alert delivery log that the T-14 and T-3 alerts were actually sent for rows whose deadlines have passed.
testing.done: recomputed freeze dates and reminder configurations agree with the recorded values, with delivery proven from the alert log.

testing.step: Test completeness against delegated entities and certification dependencies
actions: Take the delegated-entity register and confirm each delegate supplying encounter or reporting data has a feeder row on the calendar.
Check each feeder date sits at least 15 calendar days ahead of the internal freeze date.
For each sampled sweep window confirm a 42 CFR 422.504(l) certification row exists with a named certifying officer and a signed certification dated on or before the sweep date.
Flag any window submitted without a completed certification as a reportable breach rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every delegate has a compliant feeder row and every sampled window has a dated, signed data-accuracy certification.

testing.step: Test the ad hoc and RADV response rows against the CMS-stated windows
actions: For each ad hoc row compare the calendar open date to the HPMS notice date and confirm the row opened within one business day.
Compare the recorded response window to the window stated in the HPMS notice, word for word.
Trace the response submission date to the HPMS upload confirmation and confirm it fell inside the window.
Confirm Regulatory Counsel and the Medicare Compliance Officer were notified on the notice date.
testing.done: every ad hoc CMS request opened within one business day, met the stated window and shows same-day counsel notification.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception recording H-number, obligation, the deadline missed or mis-derived and the payment or program impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: memo not triaged, deadline copied from prior year, source feed late, delegate late, certification not obtained.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and for any missed CMS window open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception forward as a mandatory retest row in the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, a coded root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missed-data-call threshold and state the conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Confirm the reviewer signing the workpaper owns no H-number on the calendar and performed none of the sampled tracking.
Report the conclusion, exception rate and open breaches to the Medicare Compliance Committee at its next sitting and minute the report.
File the signed workpaper with the population extract, sample seed and CMS source captures under the payment year with a 10-year retention label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and minuted committee reporting is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns extraction and validation of the 42 CFR 422.516 Part C reporting data elements; escalation to the Data Governance Lead on unresolved element-level defects

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 42 CFR 422.516 read against the current e-CFR text and reconciled to the element definitions in the CMS Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications for the reporting year

In-scope processes.value: Element extraction and validation for each 422.516 section: organization determinations and reconsiderations, grievances, special needs plan care management, payments to providers, rewards and incentives - across every H-number and PBP

In-scope systems.value: Appeals and grievances case management, care management and claims sources staged in the warehouse; validation rules executed in the data catalog/quality tool

Compliance procedure documented.value: Part C Reporting Element Extraction and Validation Procedure - element-to-source mapping, CMS data dictionary rules, tolerance thresholds, defect triage and the validation report template

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Data Governance Lead and the Medicare Compliance Officer; re-approved whenever CMS republishes the Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Validation must complete and sign off at least 10 business days before each section's CMS-published due date in the technical specifications reporting deadline table

Deadline reminders configured.value: Validation-cycle reminders at T-30 (extract due), T-20 (rules executed), T-10 (validation report signed) counted back from each section due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Validation report, rule execution logs, defect register and reconciliation to the source of record retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each failed validation rule is logged as a data defect with element name, section, record count, root cause and disposition (corrected, sourced, accepted with CMS note)

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every accepted-with-note defect and every element released to submission with an open defect

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every 422.516 element instance extracted for the reporting period, by section, H-number and PBP, as staged for submission

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unexplained variance to the source of record on countable elements; any element failing a CMS data-dictionary rule and released without a signed disposition is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs per data call; the test runs on every extraction cycle before submission, with a full-year look-back test after the final section is filed

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have written or executed the validation rules being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-cycle validation test workpaper (extract query, rule results, source reconciliation, defect register, sign-offs) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Validation report plus element-level lineage from source system to submitted value, producible for a CMS program audit or data validation contractor review within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: Data Management supplies lineage and rule evidence; the Medicare Compliance Officer is the sole channel to the CMS Account Manager and the data validation contractor

checklist.step: Load the current CMS element definitions into the validation rule set
actions: Download the CMS Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications for the reporting year and open the section for each reportable measure.
For every data element copy the CMS definition, the required value domain, the numerator and denominator logic and the reporting period into the element register.
Diff the register against last year's version and list every changed definition, added element and retired element.
Circulate the change list to the Appeals and Grievances manager, the Care Management lead and the Regulatory Reporting Manager for impact confirmation.
checklist.done: the element register matches the current-year CMS specifications and every definition change is listed and acknowledged.

checklist.step: Map every CMS element to a named source field
actions: For each element record the source system, table and column that supplies it - for example the appeals case table for organization determination decision dates, the grievance case table for grievance category and receipt date.
Record the transformation applied (direct copy, derived, aggregated) and the exact filter that scopes the population to the reporting period and contract.
Publish the lineage in the data catalog so the path from source column to submitted value is visible without opening code.
Send any element with no identified source to the Data Governance Lead as a sourcing gap, with the section and due date attached.
checklist.done: every CMS element has a catalogued source column, transformation, scope filter and published lineage, or a raised sourcing gap.

checklist.step: Run the extraction for the reporting period
actions: Trigger the Part C reporting extraction DAG with parameters contract H-number, PBP, section and reporting period start/end.
Confirm the run reads from the frozen reporting snapshot, not live tables, so the extract is reproducible.
Capture the run id, row counts per section and the snapshot timestamp into the run log.
Fail the run and stop rather than partially load where any upstream feed is missing, and notify the Data Quality Manager the same day.
checklist.done: a completed, reproducible extraction run exists with a recorded run id, snapshot timestamp and per-section row counts.

checklist.step: Execute the CMS data-dictionary conformance rules
actions: Run the rule pack per element: not null on mandatory fields, value in the CMS-permitted code domain, date within the reporting period, decision date on or after receipt date.

Run the timeliness rules that mirror the regulation: standard organization determinations decided within 14 calendar days for service requests and expedited within 72 hours, reconsiderations within 30 days, and Part C payment reconsiderations within 60 days.
Output a rule-by-rule result with pass count, fail count and fail rate per section and H-number.
Export the failing record keys to the defect register so each failure can be traced to a case.
checklist.done: every rule has executed with counts and fail rates by section and H-number, and failing record keys are in the defect register.

checklist.step: Reconcile extracted counts to the operational source of record
actions: Ask the Appeals and Grievances manager for the operational case counts for the reporting period straight from the case management system.
Compare to the extracted counts per section, per H-number, and build a variance bridge for every difference.
Explain each variance with a named cause: out-of-period cases, dismissed cases excluded by CMS definition, cases reassigned between contracts.
Escalate any unexplained variance above 0.5 percent of the section count to the Data Quality Manager before the extract is released.
checklist.done: extracted counts reconcile to the operational source with every variance explained or escalated.

checklist.step: Validate the special needs plan care management elements separately
actions: For SNP contracts pull the care management elements: health risk assessment completion within 90 days of enrolment, individualised care plan creation, and interdisciplinary care team review dates.
Confirm each denominator is the SNP enrolled population for the reporting period from the enrolment source, not the total membership.
Test a walk-through of 10 member records end to end from enrolment date to HRA completion date to care plan date.
Return any member record with a missing or out-of-sequence date to Care Management for correction before release.
checklist.done: SNP care management elements reconcile to the SNP enrolled denominator and 10 walk-through records are date-sequenced correctly.

checklist.step: Validate the grievance categorisation against CMS categories
actions: Pull the distribution of grievances by CMS category (enrolment/disenrolment, benefit package, access, quality of care, marketing, customer service) for the reporting period.
Sample 25 grievance cases and re-read the case narrative to confirm the category and the expedited/standard flag were coded correctly.
Confirm the resolution date recorded satisfies the 30-day standard grievance timeframe and the 24-hour expedited grievance timeframe.
Send miscoded cases back to the grievance analyst for correction and re-extract before submission.
checklist.done: grievance categories and timeframes are re-verified on a 25-case sample with all miscodes corrected and re-extracted.

checklist.step: Test the elements against prior-period trend for plausibility
actions: Build a trend view of each element for the last eight reporting periods by H-number.
Flag any element moving more than 20 percent period on period, or any element whose value is exactly zero where prior periods were non-zero.
For each flag obtain a written business explanation (membership growth, benefit change, system migration) from the owning operational team.
Attach the trend chart and the explanations to the validation report.
checklist.done: every element with a material trend break carries a written business explanation attached to the validation report.

checklist.step: Triage every defect to a root cause and disposition
actions: Work the defect register top down by record count and assign each defect a root cause: source data entry, mapping error, transformation error, definition change not implemented.
Assign a disposition: correct at source and re-extract, correct in transformation and re-run, or accept with a documented note to CMS.
Name an owner and a fix date for each defect and record whether it blocks submission.
Re-run the rule pack after every correction cycle and record the new fail rate against the old one.
checklist.done: every defect has a root cause, disposition, owner, fix date and a post-correction rule re-run result.

checklist.step: Freeze the validated data set and version it
actions: Write the corrected extract into a versioned reporting table named part_c_<section>_<H-number>_<period>_v<n>.
Record the row counts, checksum and creation timestamp for the frozen version.
Revoke write access on the frozen table so no post-validation change can occur silently.
Publish the version reference to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst who will make the HPMS submission.
checklist.done: an immutable, checksummed version of the validated data set exists and its reference is published to the submitter.

checklist.step: Produce the validation report
actions: Assemble the report: element register version, extraction run id and snapshot timestamp, rule results with fail rates, source reconciliation bridge, defect register with dispositions, trend explanations and the frozen table version.
State explicitly which elements are released clean and which are released with an accepted defect, naming each.
Include the CMS specification version the rules were built from and the date it was downloaded.
Circulate to the Data Governance Lead, the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Medicare Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: a complete validation report exists naming every element's release status and the CMS specification version behind it.

checklist.step: Obtain data governance sign-off before release
actions: Read the defect register and challenge every accept-with-note disposition against the CMS element definition.
Reject release of any element whose accepted defect would misstate a CMS-reported measure and send it back for correction.
Sign the validation report with name and date, recording the frozen table version signed off.
Where sign-off is withheld, notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day so the submission plan can be reworked.
checklist.done: a dated governance signature exists against a named frozen table version, or a same-day withholding notice was issued.

checklist.step: Hand the validated data set to the submission team with a control total sheet
actions: Produce a control sheet listing per section and H-number: record count, key sums, and the top-level measure values as validated.
Hand the sheet and the frozen table reference to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and obtain a written receipt.
Agree that the submitted values will be tied back to this control sheet after upload before the submission is closed.
File the control sheet alongside the validation report.
checklist.done: the submission team holds a receipted control sheet with per-section counts and measure values tied to a frozen version.

checklist.step: Re-run validation on any late-arriving corrections
actions: Where an operational team submits a correction after freeze, open a new extract version rather than editing the frozen table.
Re-run the full rule pack and the source reconciliation on the new version - never a partial re-run.
Produce a delta note showing which measure values changed and by how much, and route it for a fresh governance sign-off.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Analyst so a resubmission decision can be made before the CMS due date.
checklist.done: every post-freeze correction produced a new version, a full rule re-run, a delta note and a fresh sign-off.

checklist.step: Archive the validation evidence for the reporting period
actions: Bundle the element register, lineage export, rule execution logs, reconciliation bridge, defect register, trend explanations, validation report and sign-offs.
File under Medicare Advantage > Part C Reporting > <reporting year> > <section> and apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the bundle is searchable by H-number, section and reporting period.
Record the archive reference on the validation report so a CMS auditor can be pointed at it directly.
checklist.done: the validation evidence bundle is filed with a 10-year label, searchable by H-number, section and period.

testing.step: Rebuild the element population independently from the source systems
actions: Write your own query against the appeals, grievance, care management and claims source tables using only the CMS definition, without reading the production extraction code.
Scope it to the same contracts, PBPs and reporting period and record the query text in the workpaper.
Produce your own record counts and measure values per section and H-number.
Sign the population with the query text, run timestamp and the snapshot used.
testing.done: an independently written population exists with recorded query text and its own per-section counts and measure values.

testing.step: Reconcile the independent build to the frozen submission version
actions: Compare your counts and measure values to the frozen table version named on the control sheet, line by line.
Build a variance bridge for every section showing the driver of each difference.
Investigate any variance above 0.5 percent of the section count to the individual record and state the cause.
Record which build is correct where they differ - do not default to the production figure.
testing.done: a completed variance bridge exists for every section with each material difference traced to individual records.

testing.step: Draw a documented record-level sample across sections
actions: Stratify by section and take 25 records per reportable section, plus 100 percent of records failing any rule but released.
Select at random with a recorded seed and note the population size per stratum.
Include at least 5 records per H-number so contract-level errors surface.
Document the seed, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a stratified, reproducible record-level sample covering every section and every released rule failure is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the element derivation on each sampled record
actions: Open the underlying case in the appeals or grievance case management system and read the receipt date, decision date, category and disposition from the case itself.
Derive the CMS element value yourself from the case facts using the technical specification definition.
Compare to the submitted value and record agreement or a difference with the reason.
Capture the case screen showing the dates relied upon into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled record has an independently derived element value, a comparison result and a captured source case screen.

testing.step: Recompute the regulatory timeliness calculations
actions: For each sampled organization determination recompute elapsed time from receipt to decision and test it against the 14-calendar-day standard service request limit and the 72-hour expedited limit.
For each sampled reconsideration recompute elapsed time against the 30-day standard limit and the 60-day payment reconsideration limit.
Confirm the extraction's day-count convention matches the CMS convention (calendar days, counted from the day after receipt) and flag any off-by-one behaviour.
List every record the production rules passed that your recomputation fails.
testing.done: timeliness calculations are recomputed on the sample with the day-count convention verified and disagreements listed.

testing.step: Test the lineage from source column to submitted value
actions: Pick 10 elements and follow the published lineage from the submitted value back to the source column.
Confirm the transformation shown in the catalog is the transformation actually running in the extraction job by reading the job code.
Flag any element whose catalogued lineage is stale, missing or contradicted by the code.
Record the lineage screenshots and the code reference for each tested element.
testing.done: 10 elements have end-to-end lineage verified against the running code, with stale entries flagged.

testing.step: Test the defect dispositions and the sign-off chain
actions: Take every defect dispositioned as accept-with-note and read the CMS definition it was accepted against.
Confirm the acceptance does not change the reported measure value materially, and quantify the effect where it does.
Confirm each accepted defect carries a dated Data Governance Lead signature that pre-dates the submission.
Treat any element released with an open defect and no signature as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every accepted defect is quantified and carries a dated pre-submission governance signature.

testing.step: Test the freeze control and post-freeze changes
actions: Recompute the checksum of the frozen table and compare it to the checksum recorded on the control sheet.
Pull the table's access grants and confirm write access was revoked at freeze.
Query the audit log for any DML against the frozen table after the freeze timestamp.
For each post-freeze correction confirm a new version, a full rule re-run and a fresh sign-off exist.
testing.done: the frozen checksum matches, write access was revoked, and every post-freeze change produced a versioned re-run and sign-off.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with section, H-number, element, records affected and the effect on the reported measure.
Assign a coded root cause: definition change not implemented, mapping error, transformation error, source data quality, control bypass.
Set an owner and remediation date, and where a submitted measure is misstated open a resubmission assessment with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Carry open exceptions into the next cycle's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, where measures are misstated, a resubmission assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-unexplained-variance threshold.
Confirm the signing reviewer wrote and executed none of the validation rules under test.
Report the conclusion, misstated measures and resubmission decisions to the Medicare Compliance Committee and minute it.
File the signed workpaper with the independent query text, sample seed and source captures under a 10-year retention label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and minuted committee reporting is filed with a 10-year retention label.

checklist.step: Confirm HPMS user access and submitter roles before the window opens
actions: In CMS HPMS open User Access > My Access and confirm the Plan Reporting Module submitter role is active for every H-number you must file for.
Confirm the backup uploader holds the same role and that both accounts have logged in within the last 60 days so neither is deactivated for inactivity.
Where access is missing, submit the HPMS user access request through the CMS Enterprise Portal and record the request date and ticket number.
Record confirmed access, role and expiry date against every calendar row that requires an HPMS upload.
checklist.done: an active primary and backup HPMS submitter exists for every H-number, evidenced by a dated access confirmation.

checklist.step: Take receipt of the validated data set and its control sheet
actions: Collect from the Data Quality Manager the frozen table version reference, the control sheet with per-section record counts and measure values, and the signed validation report.
Refuse the handoff where the validation report is unsigned or names an element released with an open, unsigned defect.
Record the version reference and the receipt date on the calendar row for the section.
Confirm the reporting period on the control sheet matches the CMS reporting period for that section.
checklist.done: a signed validation report, control sheet and frozen version reference are receipted against the correct CMS reporting period.

checklist.step: Build the submission file in the CMS-required layout
actions: Generate the file from the frozen table using the layout in the CMS Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications - field order, delimiters, date format CCYYMMDD and the required header record.
Apply the CMS file naming convention including contract number, section and reporting period, exactly as the specification states.
Verify the row count in the file trailer equals the control sheet count for that section.
Save the file to the submission staging folder with the frozen version reference in the file metadata.
checklist.done: a correctly named, correctly laid-out file exists whose trailer count equals the control sheet count.

checklist.step: Pre-validate the file before uploading it to CMS
actions: Run the format checker over the file: field lengths, permitted code values, date format, no embedded delimiters, no trailing blank rows.
Confirm the contract number in every record matches the H-number the file will be uploaded under.
Where CMS provides a test upload path, use it first and read the returned validation report rather than uploading blind to production.
Send the format-check output to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and block the upload on any hard error.
checklist.done: the file passes format checking with no hard errors and, where available, a clean CMS test upload result.

checklist.step: Upload each Part C reporting section through the HPMS Plan Reporting Module
actions: In HPMS open Plan Reporting > Part C Reporting > Data Submission and select the contract number and the reporting period.
Select the reporting section (organization determinations and reconsiderations, grievances, SNP care management, payments to providers, rewards and incentives) and attach the prepared file.
Click Submit and wait for the module to return the submission status rather than navigating away.
Repeat per H-number and per section, working the calendar rows in due-date order.
checklist.done: every due section is uploaded under the correct contract and reporting period with a returned submission status.

checklist.step: Capture the CMS confirmation for every upload
actions: Screenshot the HPMS confirmation screen showing contract number, section, reporting period, status Submitted, the confirmation number and the timestamp.
Save it as hpms-<H-number>-<section>-<period>-confirmation.pdf in the submission evidence folder.
Write the confirmation number and submission timestamp onto the data call calendar row and close the row only after both are recorded.
Where the module returns an error instead of a confirmation, leave the row open and go straight to the rejection-handling procedure.
checklist.done: every upload has a saved confirmation capture and its confirmation number and timestamp recorded on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Tie the submitted values back to the validated control sheet
actions: Re-open the submitted section in HPMS and read back the accepted record count and the top-level measure values the module displays.
Compare each to the control sheet figure and record agreement or the difference on a tie-out sheet.
Where a difference exists, do not accept it - determine whether CMS rejected records or the wrong file version was uploaded before closing the row.
Sign and date the tie-out sheet and file it with the confirmation capture.
checklist.done: a signed tie-out sheet shows every submitted measure agreeing with the validated control sheet, or the difference resolved.

checklist.step: Transmit the encounter data files through the EDFES gateway
actions: Submit the 837-I and 837-P encounter files for the sweep window using the organization's Submitter ID and the contract H-number in the ISA/GS envelope.
Confirm the TA1 interchange acknowledgement returns without a rejection, then wait for the 999 implementation acknowledgement and the 277CA claim acknowledgement.
Record the file name, interchange control number, submission timestamp and each acknowledgement receipt time in the transmission log.
Hold the sweep row open until the MAO-002 Encounter Data Processing Status Report is retrieved and its accepted counts recorded.
checklist.done: every encounter file has TA1, 999 and 277CA acknowledgements logged and an MAO-002 accepted count recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the annual bid package through the HPMS Bid Submission module
actions: In HPMS open Bid Submission > Upload Bid and select the contract year, contract number and PBP.
Attach the completed Bid Pricing Tool, the Plan Benefit Package and the actuarial certification signed by the certifying actuary.
Submit ahead of the statutory deadline in 42 CFR 422.254(a) - the first Monday in June for the following contract year - and capture the upload confirmation.
Log the confirmation number and any CMS desk review questions received afterwards, with the response due dates.
checklist.done: the bid package is uploaded before the first Monday in June with a captured confirmation and any desk review questions logged.

checklist.step: Obtain the data-accuracy certification for the submission
actions: Assemble the certification package: the submitted file summary, the validation report, the tie-out sheet and the certification statement required by 42 CFR 422.504(l).
Route it to the CEO, CFO or their documented delegate at least 5 business days before the CMS due date.
Obtain the signature attesting the data is accurate, complete and truthful based on best knowledge, information and belief.
File the executed certification with the submission evidence and record the signature date on the calendar row.
checklist.done: an executed 422.504(l) certification, signed on or before the CMS due date, is filed with the submission evidence.

checklist.step: Monitor for CMS post-submission feedback and correction windows
actions: Check HPMS Plan Reporting > Submission History daily for the week after each upload and read any status change from Submitted to Accepted or Returned.
Read every CMS feedback report or data validation finding and log it against the section with the correction window stated by CMS.
Confirm whether the section is still inside its CMS correction window before deciding to resubmit versus wait for the next cycle.
Notify the Data Quality Manager the same day a return or finding is received.
checklist.done: each submission's status is monitored daily for a week and every CMS finding is logged with its correction window.

checklist.step: Escalate any submission that will miss its CMS due date
actions: Where the T-5 alert fires with the file not ready, raise the escalation to the Medicare Compliance Officer and the owning operational lead the same day.
Present the affected H-numbers and sections, the cause, the earliest realistic submission date and the program consequence.
Decide and record: submit a partial file inside the window with a follow-up, or notify the CMS Account Manager of a late submission with a firm date.
Never allow a due date to pass without either a submission or a dated CMS notification.
checklist.done: every at-risk submission has a same-day escalation, a recorded decision and either a submission or a dated CMS notification.

checklist.step: Update the submission log and close the calendar row
actions: Write one log row per submission: H-number, section, reporting period, file name and version, upload timestamp, confirmation number, accepted counts, certification date and uploader.
Link the row to the confirmation capture, tie-out sheet and certification in the evidence repository.
Set the calendar row to Closed only when confirmation number, tie-out and certification are all present.
Report the week's closures and any open rows to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the submission log holds one complete, evidence-linked row per submission and only fully evidenced rows are closed.

checklist.step: Debrief each submission cycle and feed fixes upstream
actions: Within 10 business days of the cycle close, hold a debrief with Data Management, Appeals and Grievances and Care Management.
Review every rejected record, late file and tie-out difference and assign a preventive action with an owner and a date.
Record the actual versus planned dates for extract, validation, upload and certification so the back-schedule can be tightened.
Minute the debrief and carry open actions into the next cycle's plan.
checklist.done: a minuted debrief exists with owned preventive actions and actual-versus-planned cycle timings recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the submission evidence pack
actions: Bundle per section and H-number: submitted file, HPMS confirmation capture, tie-out sheet, certification, transmission log and any CMS feedback.
File under Medicare Advantage > Submissions > <reporting year> and apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the pack is retrievable by confirmation number, H-number and reporting period.
Record the archive reference on the submission log row.
checklist.done: a per-section submission pack is archived with a 10-year label and retrievable by confirmation number.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions that were due in the period
actions: Take the CMS reporting deadline table and the risk adjustment sweep schedule and expand them across every active H-number and PBP to derive what was due.
Add the annual bid submission for each contract and PBP offered in the following contract year.
Do not build the population from the submission log - the log is the control being tested.
Sign the population stating the CMS sources, the contract list used and the extraction date.
testing.done: a signed, CMS-derived population of what was due exists, built independently of the submission log.

testing.step: Reconcile the due population to the submission log
actions: Match each due item to a submission log row on H-number + section + reporting period.
List every due item with no log row as a potential unfiled submission and pursue it to a confirmation number or an exception.
List every log row with no matching due item and confirm it was a legitimate voluntary or corrected filing.
Show the reconciliation bridge and the resolved counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: every due item is matched to a log row or raised as a potential unfiled submission, with a documented bridge.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100 percent of bid submissions and 100 percent of risk adjustment sweep transmissions.
Take 20 rows selected at random with a recorded seed from the 422.516 section submissions, spread across all H-numbers.
Record the seed, strata, population size and selection date.
Add as mandatory rows every submission already known to have been returned or rejected by CMS.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is documented covering all bids, all sweeps and a seeded selection of section submissions.

testing.step: Re-perform the confirmation lookup directly in HPMS
actions: In HPMS open Plan Reporting > Submission History for the sampled contract and reporting period.
Read the status, confirmation number and submission timestamp from the module itself rather than from the saved capture.
Compare all three to the submission log row and to the saved confirmation capture; any mismatch is an exception.
Capture the HPMS history screen into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled submission is confirmed directly in HPMS with status, confirmation number and timestamp matching the log.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness against the CMS due date
actions: For each sampled row take the CMS due date from the specification deadline table, not from the calendar row.
Compare the HPMS submission timestamp to that due date and compute days early or late.
For bid submissions confirm the upload timestamp precedes the first Monday in June deadline under 42 CFR 422.254(a).
For encounter sweeps confirm the transmission and its 277CA acceptance both fall inside the sweep window.
testing.done: days early or late is computed for every sampled submission against the CMS-published due date.

testing.step: Trace submitted values back to the validated data set
actions: For each sampled section pull the submitted file from the archive and recompute its record count and top-level measure values.
Compare to the control sheet issued by validation and to the counts HPMS displays as accepted.
Confirm the archived file's version reference matches the frozen table version named on the signed validation report.
Flag any submission whose file version does not match the version that was validated and signed.
testing.done: every sampled submitted file ties to the validated control sheet and to the signed frozen version reference.

testing.step: Test the encounter acknowledgement chain end to end
actions: For each sampled encounter transmission retrieve the TA1, 999 and 277CA and confirm each references the same interchange control number as the submitted file.
Retrieve the MAO-002 and compare accepted, rejected and pending counts to the transmission log entry.
Confirm the rejected count was routed to the rejection-handling process with a case reference.
Flag any transmission logged as complete without a retrievable 277CA.
testing.done: every sampled transmission has a complete, control-number-matched acknowledgement chain and its MAO-002 counts reconciled.

testing.step: Test the certification and access controls behind the submissions
actions: For each sampled submission confirm an executed 42 CFR 422.504(l) certification exists, signed by the CEO, CFO or a documented delegate, dated on or before the due date.
Where a delegate signed, read the delegation document and confirm it was in force on the signature date.
Extract the HPMS submitter role list and confirm the person shown as uploader in HPMS held the role at the upload timestamp.
Flag any submission uploaded by an account without an active submitter role.
testing.done: every sampled submission has a valid, in-force certification and was uploaded by an authorised HPMS submitter.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with H-number, section, due date, actual submission date and the program impact.
Assign a coded root cause: access lapse, file format rejection, validation late, wrong file version, certification not obtained, deadline mis-derived.
Set an owner and remediation date; for any missed CMS due date open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the Medicare Compliance Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, for missed deadlines, a self-disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-late, zero-unconfirmed threshold and state the conclusion.
Confirm the signing reviewer holds no HPMS submitter role and performed none of the sampled uploads.
Report late submissions, unfiled sections and any self-disclosure to the Medicare Compliance Committee and minute the report.
File the signed workpaper with the CMS-derived due population, sample seed and HPMS captures under a 10-year retention label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and minuted committee reporting is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Retrieve the CMS rejection reports as soon as they are published
actions: Download from the EDPS mailbox the MAO-002 Encounter Data Processing Status Report and the MAO-004 risk-filtering report for each submitted file.
Download the 277CA claim acknowledgement and the 999 implementation acknowledgement for the same interchange control numbers.
Load all reports into the rejection staging table keyed on interchange control number, ICN, contract H-number and error code.
Alert the Data Quality Manager the same day the reports land and record the retrieval timestamp.
checklist.done: all MAO-002, MAO-004, 277CA and 999 reports for the file are loaded and keyed, with a recorded retrieval timestamp.

checklist.step: Triage every rejection by CMS error code
actions: Join the rejected records to the CMS edit code list and label each code as format/syntax, eligibility, duplicate, provider identifier, diagnosis code validity or linkage to a prior encounter.
Rank the codes by rejected record count and by estimated risk-adjustable diagnosis count so the highest-value defects are worked first.
Assign each code group to an owning team: Data Management for format and linkage, Claims Operations for provider and diagnosis data, Enrolment for eligibility mismatches.
Publish the triage table to the Data Quality Manager and the owning team leads within one business day of report retrieval.
checklist.done: every rejected record carries a labelled error code group, an owning team and a position in the ranked triage table.

checklist.step: Open a remediation case per error-code group and start the 30-day clock
actions: Create one case per error code per H-number holding: code, description, rejected record count, dates of service span, owning team and the report date.
Set the case due date at 30 days from the rejection report date, and set a hard stop 10 days before the sweep window closes, whichever is earlier.
Attach the record key list so the owning team can work the actual encounters rather than a summary.
Configure the day-7, day-20 and day-27 alerts on the case.
checklist.done: every error-code group has a case with a 30-day due date, a sweep-window hard stop, attached record keys and alerts set.

checklist.step: Trace each rejection back to the originating source record
actions: For a sample of at least 20 records per error code, open the originating claim in the claims platform using the ICN and read the fields the edit rejected.
Record whether the defect exists in the source claim, was introduced by the mapping into the 837, or reflects a CMS reference-data mismatch.
Where the defect is in the source claim, identify the intake channel (provider EDI, delegated entity file, manual entry) so the fix lands upstream.
Write the finding onto the case with the specific field name and an example ICN.
checklist.done: each error code has a documented origin - source claim, mapping or reference data - with named fields and example ICNs.

checklist.step: Fix format and mapping defects in the submission build
actions: Amend the 837 mapping for the failing segment or loop - for example the rendering provider NPI in loop 2310B or the service facility address in 2310C.
Add a pre-submission rule to the format checker that would have caught the defect, so the same code cannot recur silently.
Re-run the extraction for the affected records only, producing a correction file rather than a full resubmission.
Record the code change reference, the new rule id and the correction file name on the case.
checklist.done: the mapping is amended, a preventive pre-submission rule is added, and a correction file exists referenced on the case.

checklist.step: Correct eligibility and enrolment mismatch rejections
actions: For records rejected because the beneficiary was not enrolled with the contract on the date of service, compare the encounter date of service to the CMS Monthly Membership Report enrolment span.
Where the encounter is genuinely outside the enrolment span, mark the record as correctly rejected and record the reason - do not resubmit it.
Where enrolment data is stale, request the enrolment correction from the Enrolment team and record the expected effective date of the fix.
Hold affected records until the enrolment correction is confirmed, then release them into the next correction file.
checklist.done: every eligibility rejection is either evidenced as correctly rejected or held pending a confirmed enrolment correction.

checklist.step: Work provider and diagnosis validity rejections with Claims Operations
actions: For invalid or non-specific diagnosis code rejections, re-read the source claim and the supporting documentation and confirm the code is valid for the date of service under the applicable ICD-10-CM version.
For provider identifier rejections, verify the NPI and taxonomy against the NPPES registry and the internal provider master, and correct the master where it is wrong.
Never substitute a diagnosis code that is not documented in the medical record - record the encounter as unrecoverable instead.
Return corrected records to the Data Engineer for inclusion in the correction file and note the verification source on the case.
checklist.done: every provider and diagnosis rejection is corrected against a verified source or recorded as unrecoverable with the reason.

checklist.step: Resolve duplicate and linkage rejections
actions: For duplicate rejections, confirm against the EDPS accepted history whether the original encounter was already accepted, using the ICN and the CMS-assigned encounter ID.
Close records whose original is confirmed accepted, recording the accepted encounter ID as the evidence - resubmitting them creates a second defect.
For chart review or adjustment records rejected on linkage, correct the linked internal control number reference to the CMS encounter ID of the accepted original.
Record the accepted encounter ID and the corrected linkage on each record.
checklist.done: duplicate rejections are closed against a confirmed accepted encounter ID and linkage errors carry a corrected reference.

checklist.step: Approve the correction file before resubmission
actions: Review the correction file summary: record count by error code, records dropped as correctly rejected, records held for enrolment correction.
Confirm every dropped record has a written reason and no record was dropped purely because it was hard to fix.
Confirm the preventive rule for each error code has been added to the pre-submission checker.
Sign the correction file for release, naming the file and the record count.
checklist.done: a dated governance signature releases a named correction file with every dropped record justified in writing.

checklist.step: Resubmit the correction file and confirm acceptance
actions: Transmit the correction file through EDFES with the correct claim frequency code for a replacement or void, and a new interchange control number.
Confirm the TA1, 999 and 277CA return clean for the correction file and record the receipt times.
Retrieve the next MAO-002 and confirm the previously rejected records now show accepted, recording the CMS encounter IDs.
Update each case with the accepted counts and the residual rejects that need a second correction cycle.
checklist.done: the correction file is transmitted, acknowledged, and its acceptance confirmed on the next MAO-002 with residual rejects re-cased.

checklist.step: Handle HPMS returned Part C reporting submissions
actions: Where HPMS Plan Reporting > Submission History shows a section Returned, read the CMS return reason and the correction window stated in the notice.
Open a case within one business day and route the correction to the owning operational team with the CMS window as the due date.
Rebuild the section file from a fresh validated version rather than editing the returned file.
Re-upload through Plan Reporting > Part C Reporting > Data Submission and capture the new confirmation number and timestamp.
checklist.done: every returned HPMS section is re-cased within one business day and re-uploaded inside the CMS-stated correction window.

checklist.step: Track case ageing against the 30-day correction service level
actions: Publish a weekly ageing view: open cases by error code, days since the rejection report, records outstanding and days to the sweep-window hard stop.
Highlight every case past day 20 and every case whose records would miss the sweep window.
Chase the owning team lead in writing on each highlighted case and record the response.
Report the ageing view to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Medicare Compliance Officer weekly.
checklist.done: a weekly ageing view is published, every case past day 20 is chased in writing, and the report is issued to compliance.

checklist.step: Escalate unrecoverable rejections and service-level breaches
actions: Take every case that will breach 30 days or the sweep-window hard stop and assess the risk score and revenue impact with the Actuarial Analyst.
Where records are genuinely unrecoverable - no supporting documentation, provider no longer contracted - record the disposition and the quantified impact.
Decide whether the volume or pattern requires notification to the CMS Account Manager, and obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance before any notification.
Sign the disposition and record it on the case; abandoning records silently is never permitted.
checklist.done: every breach or unrecoverable case has a quantified impact, a signed disposition and a documented notification decision.

checklist.step: Close the loop with a preventive action per recurring error code
actions: Monthly, list every error code that appeared in two or more consecutive rejection reports.
For each, agree a preventive action with the owning team - intake edit at the provider portal, delegated-entity file specification change, master data correction, mapping fix.
Set an owner and a target date and track it to closure alongside the operational cases.
Measure the code's rejection rate the month after the fix and record whether the action worked.
checklist.done: every recurring error code has an owned preventive action with a post-fix rejection rate measured.

checklist.step: Archive the rejection and remediation evidence
actions: Bundle per sweep window: MAO-002 and MAO-004 reports, 277CA files, rejection cases with root cause and disposition, correction files, resubmission acknowledgements and sign-offs.
File under Medicare Advantage > Encounter Data > <payment year> and apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm retrieval by H-number, error code, ICN and CMS encounter ID.
Record the archive reference on each closed case.
checklist.done: the rejection remediation bundle is archived with a 10-year label and retrievable by ICN and CMS encounter ID.

testing.step: Build the rejection population straight from the CMS reports
actions: Pull every MAO-002, MAO-004 and 277CA report issued in the period directly from the EDPS mailbox, not from the rejection staging table.
Extract the rejected and pending record counts by contract H-number and error code, and add every HPMS section showing status Returned.
Record the report dates, interchange control numbers and the retrieval date.
Sign the population as complete stating the reports relied on.
testing.done: a signed population of rejections is built directly from CMS reports with counts by H-number and error code.

testing.step: Reconcile the CMS reports to the rejection case register
actions: Match rejected record counts per error code per H-number to the case register totals.
List error codes present in the CMS reports with no case opened and pursue each to an explanation or an exception.
Confirm each case's start date equals the rejection report date, not the date the team noticed it.
Present the reconciliation bridge with the unmatched counts resolved.
testing.done: CMS rejection counts reconcile to the case register with every untriaged error code raised as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of rejection cases and records
actions: Take 100 percent of cases breaching 30 days and 100 percent of records dispositioned as unrecoverable.
Take 15 cases at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, and within each case 10 records at random.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and the selection date.
State why any error-code stratum was excluded.
testing.done: a stratified, reproducible sample covering all breaches and all unrecoverable dispositions is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the error triage on the sampled records
actions: Look up each sampled record's CMS error code in the current CMS edit code list and read the code description yourself.
Reach your own conclusion on the defect category and the owning team before reading the case triage.
Compare to the recorded triage; a mis-categorised code that sent the case to the wrong team is an exception even where the record was eventually fixed.
Capture the edit code list entry relied upon into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent triage conclusion compared against the recorded one, with the code list captured.

testing.step: Trace sampled records to the source claim and the correction
actions: Open each sampled record's originating claim by ICN and read the field the edit rejected.
Confirm the correction actually applied matches the defect found - not a workaround that suppresses the edit without fixing the data.
For diagnosis corrections confirm the substituted code is supported by documentation referenced on the case; an unsupported change is a reportable finding, not an exception.
Capture the claim screen and the correction record into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled correction is traced to the source claim and confirmed to fix the actual defect with documented support.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day correction clock and sweep-window headroom
actions: For each sampled case recompute elapsed days from the CMS rejection report date to the resubmission acknowledgement date.
Compare to the 30-day service level and compute the on-time rate against the 95 percent threshold.
Recompute headroom to the sweep-window close for every case and list any records resubmitted after the window closed.
Confirm the day-7, day-20 and day-27 alerts fired from the alert delivery log for cases that ran past those points.
testing.done: elapsed days, on-time rate and sweep-window headroom are recomputed, with alert firing evidenced from the delivery log.

testing.step: Verify acceptance of resubmitted records on the following MAO-002
actions: For each sampled corrected record find it on the next MAO-002 and confirm status accepted with a CMS-assigned encounter ID.
Confirm the correction file used the correct replacement or void frequency code so the original was superseded rather than duplicated.
Check the MAO-004 to confirm risk-adjustable diagnoses on the corrected record were filtered in as expected.
Flag any record recorded as corrected on the case but never accepted by CMS.
testing.done: every sampled corrected record is confirmed accepted with a CMS encounter ID, or flagged as corrected-but-not-accepted.

testing.step: Test the disposition of dropped and unrecoverable records
actions: Read the written reason for every record dropped as correctly rejected or unrecoverable in the sample.
For eligibility drops re-check the date of service against the CMS Monthly Membership Report enrolment span yourself.
For duplicate drops confirm the cited accepted encounter ID actually exists in the EDPS accepted history.
Confirm each unrecoverable disposition carries a dated Compliance Officer signature and a quantified impact.
testing.done: every dropped record's reason is independently verified and every unrecoverable disposition is signed and quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording H-number, error code, records affected, days over service level and the risk score impact.
Assign a coded root cause: report not retrieved, code mis-triaged, owning team unresponsive, fix suppressed the edit rather than the defect, record abandoned without sign-off.
Set an owner and remediation date; where records missed the sweep window entirely, open a payment-impact assessment with Actuarial and Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, for missed sweeps, a payment-impact assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds: zero unsigned abandonments, 95 percent corrected within 30 days, 100 percent resolved before the sweep window.
Confirm the signing reviewer worked and approved none of the sampled cases.
Report the on-time rate, recurring error codes and any records lost to the sweep window to the Medicare Compliance Committee and minute it.
File the signed workpaper with the CMS report extracts, sample seed and claim captures under a 10-year retention label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and minuted committee reporting is filed in the repository.
