checklist.step: Define the Medicare Advantage record classes and their retention clocks
actions: List each record class: HPMS submission files and confirmations, encounter 837 files and acknowledgements, MAO-002/MAO-004 reports, validation reports, data-accuracy certifications, bid packages, rejection cases, and the underlying claim and appeal case files.
For each class set the clock start under 42 CFR 422.504(d): 10 years from the final date of the contract period or from the completion of any audit or investigation, whichever is later.
Record the system of record, the archive location and the responsible custodian for each class.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm in writing that each clock start is correctly derived before the schedule is published.
checklist.done: a published record schedule names every class, its clock start, custodian and archive location, with written counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Apply retention labels at the point the artefact is filed
actions: Configure the repository so filing into Medicare Advantage > Submissions applies the MA-10YR retention label automatically.
Set the label to block deletion and to block edit-in-place so a filed confirmation cannot be altered.
Require the metadata fields H-number, section, reporting period, submission date and confirmation number before an item can be saved.
Test the configuration by attempting to delete a test item and confirming the repository refuses.
checklist.done: auto-labelling and delete-blocking are configured and proven by a failed test deletion, with mandatory metadata enforced.

checklist.step: Build the per-submission artefact completeness checklist
actions: For every submission define the required artefact set: submitted file, HPMS confirmation capture, tie-out sheet, signed validation report, 422.504(l) certification, and for encounters the 999/277CA/MAO-002.
Add the artefact checklist to the submission log row so a row cannot be closed with an artefact missing.
Run the checklist immediately after each submission closes rather than at year end.
Route any missing artefact back to the producing team with a 5-business-day recovery date.
checklist.done: every closed submission row shows a complete artefact checklist, with any gap routed for 5-day recovery.

checklist.step: Retain the supporting detail behind the reported numbers, not just the submissions
actions: Register the frozen reporting tables (part_c_<section>_<H-number>_<period>_v<n>) as retained objects and block their drop for 10 years.
Snapshot the source appeal, grievance and care management case extracts used for each period so the reported figure can be rebuilt.
Record the checksum and row count of each retained object in the archive index so silent change is detectable.
Confirm with the platform team that the retention policy survives warehouse migrations and storage tier changes.
checklist.done: every frozen reporting table and its source snapshot is registered as retained, checksummed and protected from drop.

checklist.step: Retain the medical records supporting risk-adjusted diagnoses
actions: For every chart review encounter submitted, file the source medical record page images against the CMS encounter ID and the date of service.
Index by beneficiary HICN/MBI, provider NPI, date of service and diagnosis code so a RADV request can be answered by sample line.
Confirm each record carries a legible provider signature and credential, since an unsigned record cannot support a RADV-validated diagnosis.
Apply the MA-10YR label and record the index reference on the encounter.
checklist.done: every chart-review-supported diagnosis has an indexed, signed medical record filed under a 10-year label.

checklist.step: Maintain the archive index and prove retrievability
actions: Publish an index listing every archived artefact by H-number, section, reporting period, artefact type and retrieval path.
Reconcile the index monthly to the submission log so a submission cannot exist without indexed artefacts.
Record the index version and the reconciliation result each month.
Escalate any submission with indexed artefacts missing to the Medicare Compliance Officer within 5 business days.
checklist.done: a monthly reconciled index exists linking every submission to its artefacts, with gaps escalated within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Run a quarterly retrieval drill against the CMS 3-day universe window
actions: Pick 10 archived submissions at random across H-numbers and reporting periods without warning the custodians.
Request the full artefact set as a CMS program audit would, and start a clock at the request time.
Record the elapsed time to a complete, legible, correctly indexed production for each request.
Fail any request that exceeds 3 business days or returns an incomplete set, and raise the gap for remediation.
checklist.done: a quarterly drill record shows retrieval time and completeness for 10 unannounced requests against the 3-day standard.

checklist.step: Operate the legal hold register
actions: On notice of a CMS program audit, RADV audit, OIG or DOJ enquiry, or litigation, issue a written hold naming the record classes, H-numbers and date ranges.
Register the hold in the repository so the destruction job cannot act on held records, and confirm the block by attempting a test disposition.
Notify every custodian in writing and collect acknowledgements within 5 business days.
Review open holds quarterly and release only in writing when the matter is formally closed.
checklist.done: every hold is registered, technically enforced, acknowledged by custodians and reviewed quarterly.

checklist.step: Control delegated-entity and vendor record retention
actions: Confirm each delegated entity and vendor contract carries the 42 CFR 422.504(i) downstream flow-down requiring 10-year retention and CMS access rights.
Obtain annual written attestation from each delegate that the records exist and are retrievable, naming the storage location.
For any delegate terminating, execute the record transfer or escrow before the contract ends and record the transfer manifest.
Log any delegate unable to attest as a third-party risk finding with a remediation date.
checklist.done: every delegate has a flow-down clause, a current annual attestation, and a transfer manifest where the relationship ended.

checklist.step: Run the annual disposition review before anything is destroyed
actions: Each January produce the list of records reaching the end of their 10-year clock during the year, by class and H-number.
Filter out anything under a legal hold or connected to an audit that has not been formally completed.
Recompute each item's clock start against the contract period end date and any later audit completion date - never trust the stored date alone.
Issue the proposed destruction list to the Medicare Compliance Officer and Regulatory Counsel with a 90-day review window.
checklist.done: an annual disposition list exists with clock starts recomputed, holds excluded, and a 90-day review issued.

checklist.step: Obtain approval and execute defensible destruction
actions: Review the disposition list line by line and confirm no item relates to an open CMS, OIG or RADV matter.
Sign the destruction authorisation naming the record classes, date ranges and item counts.
Have the repository execute destruction and produce a certificate of destruction listing item identifiers, method and date.
File the certificate under a 10-year label and record it against the archive index entries removed.
checklist.done: destruction executed only under a signed authorisation, with a filed certificate listing identifiers, method and date.

checklist.step: Protect the archive through system migrations and decommissions
actions: Before any claims, case management or warehouse platform is decommissioned, identify the Medicare Advantage records it holds and their remaining retention years.
Migrate the records with their metadata and retention labels intact, and reconcile record counts and checksums before and after.
Prove retrievability on the target platform with a 10-item sample before the source is switched off.
Obtain Records Manager and Compliance Officer sign-off on the migration reconciliation before decommission proceeds.
checklist.done: no platform is decommissioned without a reconciled, sampled record migration signed by Records Management and Compliance.

checklist.step: Report retention health to the compliance committee
actions: Publish quarterly metrics: artefact completeness rate by submission, retrieval drill pass rate, open archive gaps, open holds and their age.
Show trend against the prior four quarters and name the owner of every open gap.
Present to the Medicare Compliance Committee and minute the discussion.
Raise a GRC issue for any metric outside tolerance with an owner and a remediation date.
checklist.done: quarterly retention metrics with trend and named owners are presented and minuted at the compliance committee.

checklist.step: Refresh the schedule when the regulation or contract structure changes
actions: Re-read 42 CFR 422.504(d) and the CMS program audit protocol annually and on any Federal Register final rule touching Part C record requirements.
Where a contract is novated, non-renewed or terminated, recompute the clock start for every class tied to that H-number.
Issue a schedule change notice naming the affected classes and the new clock starts, and have Records Management re-label the affected items.
File the annual review memorandum as evidence the schedule was verified, not assumed.
checklist.done: an annual counsel review memorandum exists and every contract change has produced recomputed clock starts and re-labelling.

checklist.step: Close each contract year with a completeness attestation
actions: After the final submission of the contract year, run the artefact checklist across every submission for the year.
Confirm the archive index holds every artefact and every frozen reporting table for the year.
Attest in writing that the year's records are complete, labelled and retrievable, naming any known gap and its remediation date.
File the attestation with the year's archive bundle and report it to the Medicare Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: a signed year-end completeness attestation is filed with the archive bundle, naming any residual gap and its remediation date.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions requiring retained evidence
actions: Derive from the CMS reporting deadline table and the sweep schedule every submission that should exist for the retention window, by H-number and period.
Add every bid submission and every RADV or program audit response in the window.
Do not build from the archive index - the index is the control under test.
Sign the population stating the CMS sources and contract list used.
testing.done: a signed, CMS-derived population of submissions requiring evidence exists, built independently of the archive index.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the archive index and artefact checklists
actions: Match each population item to an archive index entry on H-number + section + reporting period.
For each match confirm the index lists the full artefact set: file, confirmation, tie-out, validation report, certification and acknowledgements.
List every missing submission and every incomplete artefact set separately and pursue each to recovery or exception.
Present the completeness matrix by H-number and artefact type.
testing.done: a completeness matrix exists showing every submission's artefact set as complete, recovered or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and include the full destruction batch
actions: Take 25 submissions at random with a recorded seed, spread across all H-numbers and at least five reporting periods.
Take 100 percent of items on the year's destruction list and 100 percent of records under legal hold.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and the selection date.
Add any submission previously reported as having an archive gap as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is documented covering 25 submissions plus the entire destruction batch and hold population.

testing.step: Re-perform an unannounced retrieval against the 3-day standard
actions: Issue retrieval requests for the sampled submissions to the custodians without prior notice, timestamping each request.
Receive the artefacts and record the elapsed business days and whether the set was complete and legible.
Open each returned confirmation capture and verify it shows contract number, section, period, status and confirmation number - not a blank or cropped screenshot.
Fail any retrieval over 3 business days or with an unusable artefact and record the reason.
testing.done: each sampled retrieval has a timed, unannounced result with completeness and legibility assessed against the 3-day standard.

testing.step: Test retention labels and immutability on the sampled artefacts
actions: Extract the retention label, clock start and computed disposition date for each sampled artefact.
Recompute the disposition date as clock start plus 10 years and compare to the stored value; a shortened clock is a fail.
Attempt a controlled test edit and delete on two sampled artefacts using a standard user account and confirm both are refused.
Query the repository audit log for any successful delete or overwrite of an MA-10YR labelled item in the period.
testing.done: labels and clocks recompute correctly, edit and delete attempts are refused, and no successful deletion appears in the audit log.

testing.step: Test that the supporting detail can rebuild the reported figures
actions: For five sampled submissions read the retained frozen reporting table and recompute the top-level measure values.
Compare to the values in the archived submitted file and the tie-out sheet.
Verify the retained object's checksum and row count against the archive index entry to prove it has not changed since filing.
Flag any submission whose supporting table has been dropped, altered or tiered to unreadable storage.
testing.done: five submissions are rebuilt from retained detail with matching values and verified checksums.

testing.step: Test the legal hold register and its technical enforcement
actions: Read every open hold and confirm it names record classes, H-numbers and date ranges rather than a general instruction.
For three holds attempt a test disposition on a held item and confirm the system blocks it.
Confirm custodian acknowledgements were collected within 5 business days of issue and that quarterly reviews are minuted.
Confirm no released hold was released other than in writing by Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every hold is specific, technically enforced, acknowledged on time and released only in writing.

testing.step: Test the destruction batch before it executes
actions: For every item on the destruction list recompute the clock start against the contract period end date and any audit completion date on file.
Cross-check each item against the legal hold register and the open CMS, OIG and RADV matter list.
Confirm the signed destruction authorisation exists, names the classes, date ranges and counts, and pre-dates the scheduled execution.
Block the batch and raise a finding on any item whose recomputed clock has not expired.
testing.done: every destruction item has an independently recomputed expired clock, no hold match, and a pre-dated signed authorisation.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with H-number, record class, artefact missing or unretrievable, and the CMS audit exposure.
Assign a coded root cause: artefact never filed, label misapplied, clock start wrong, migration loss, delegate failure, hold not enforced.
Set an owner and remediation date; for any destruction inside the 10-year window notify Regulatory Counsel the same day and open a disclosure assessment.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, for premature destruction, same-day counsel notification.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds: 100 percent artefact completeness, 3-business-day retrieval, zero premature destruction.
Confirm the signing reviewer holds no write access to the archive and administers no retention labels.
Report completeness rate, retrieval failures and any premature destruction to the Medicare Compliance Committee and minute it.
File the signed workpaper with the CMS-derived population, sample seed, retrieval timings and label extracts under a 10-year label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, completeness rate and minuted committee reporting is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Load the current-year NAIC blank and instruction changes
actions: Download the NAIC Health Annual Statement Blank and Instructions for the statement year and the annual statement blank change summary.
Apply the vendor software release that carries the current-year blank and confirm the version number in Help > About matches the NAIC release.
List every changed line, new column and retired exhibit affecting Medicare reporting and assign an owner to each change.
Circulate the change list to the Controller, the Appointed Actuary and the Medicare finance lead before the close begins.
checklist.done: the reporting software carries the current-year blank version and every Medicare-relevant blank change has a named owner.

checklist.step: Confirm the reporting entity structure and Medicare line of business
actions: List each legal entity writing Medicare Advantage, its NAIC company code, its state of domicile and the H-numbers it holds.
Confirm with the Medicare Compliance Officer that the H-number to legal entity mapping is current, including any mid-year novation.
Confirm the Medicare line-of-business code used in the Analysis of Operations by Lines of Business matches the NAIC instruction for Title XVIII Medicare.
Record the entity and line-of-business mapping as the basis for every allocation in the blank.
checklist.done: a confirmed entity, NAIC code, H-number and Medicare line-of-business mapping is recorded before allocation begins.

checklist.step: Close the general ledger and lock the statutory trial balance
actions: Complete the statutory close checklist and post all Medicare-related accruals: incurred but not reported claims, risk adjustment accrual, Part C premium receivable and the CMS payment settlement accrual.
Close the period in the ledger and lock posting so the trial balance cannot move under the blank.
Export the locked statutory trial balance with account, entity and line-of-business dimensions and record its extract timestamp.
Publish the locked trial balance reference to everyone preparing blank pages.
checklist.done: the period is closed and locked, and a timestamped statutory trial balance is published as the single source for the blank.

checklist.step: Map the trial balance to blank lines and populate the core pages
actions: Load the trial balance through the mapping table into the Assets page, Liabilities Capital and Surplus page, and the Statement of Revenue and Expenses.
Review the unmapped-account report and clear every unmapped account before proceeding - never let the software default it to Other.
Confirm the Medicare column in the Analysis of Operations by Lines of Business picks up the correct line-of-business dimension.
Print the mapping exception report and file it with the close pack.
checklist.done: the blank's core pages are populated from the locked trial balance with a zero-item unmapped-account report.

checklist.step: Build the Medicare premium and member-month figures
actions: Take the CMS Monthly Membership Report and the Monthly Payment Report for each month of the period and total member months and capitation revenue by H-number.

Enter member months and premium into the Exhibit of Premiums, Enrolment and Utilization under the Medicare line.
Attach the reconciliation to the exhibit workpaper with the CMS report references.
checklist.done: Medicare member months and premium in the exhibit reconcile to the CMS Monthly Membership and Payment Reports with differences explained.

checklist.step: Build the Medicare claims and utilization figures
actions: Extract paid claims by service category (hospital inpatient, outpatient, professional, other) for the Medicare line from the claims platform for the period.
Reconcile the extract total to the claims expense posted in the ledger and clear any difference to a named cause (voids, cash timing, capitation not in claims).
Populate the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2 and the utilization columns of the Exhibit of Premiums, Enrolment and Utilization with the service-category split.
Attach the claims-to-GL reconciliation to the close pack.
checklist.done: claims by service category tie to the ledger with named differences and populate the utilization exhibit.

checklist.step: Populate Schedule H and the Medicare accident and health detail
actions: Complete Schedule H Part 1 for the Medicare line with premiums earned, claims incurred, cost containment expense and general administrative expense.
Complete Schedule H Part 2 claim reserve and liability detail and Part 3 the claim payment development by incurral year.
Confirm the Medicare column totals agree to the Statement of Revenue and Expenses and to the Analysis of Operations Medicare column.
Record the tie-out on the Schedule H workpaper.
checklist.done: Schedule H Medicare columns are complete and agree to the revenue statement and Analysis of Operations.

checklist.step: Take in the actuarial reserve figures and lock them into the blank
actions: Provide the Medicare unpaid claim liability, claim adjustment expense reserve and premium deficiency reserve as at the statement date, with the supporting development triangles.
Confirm in writing the figures reflect the Part C benefits actually required under 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b), including basic benefits consistent with national and local coverage determinations.
Reconcile the reserve handed over to the amount posted in the ledger and to the blank line, and sign the handover.
Flag any reserve movement above the materiality threshold to the Controller and the Chief Financial Officer before the blank is locked.
checklist.done: signed actuarial reserve figures tie to the ledger and the blank, with material movements flagged before lock.

checklist.step: Complete Schedule T and the state allocation of Medicare premium
actions: Allocate Medicare premium to states using the member's county of residence from the CMS Monthly Membership Report, not the plan's domicile.
Populate Schedule T Exhibit of Premiums Written by state and confirm the grand total equals the premium on the Statement of Revenue and Expenses.
List the states where the entity holds a certificate of authority and confirm no premium is allocated to a state where it is not licensed.
Attach the county-to-state allocation workbook to the schedule.
checklist.done: Schedule T totals agree to reported premium and no premium is allocated to an unlicensed state.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC cross-checks and clear every failure
actions: Run the software's full validation suite: NAIC cross-checks, prior-year comparison edits, and the electronic filing validation.
Work every failure to a fix or a documented explanation, recording the check number, the amount and the resolution.
Re-run the suite after each fix and keep re-running until the failure list holds only explained items.
Print the final validation report and file it with the close pack.
checklist.done: the final validation report shows no unexplained cross-check failure, with each explained item documented by check number.

checklist.step: Perform the analytical review before sign-off
actions: Compare each Medicare blank line to the prior period and prior year and compute the variance in amount and percentage.
Obtain a written explanation for every variance above the materiality threshold and for any line moving in an unexpected direction.
Compute and review the Medicare loss ratio, administrative expense ratio and per-member-per-month claim cost against plan and prior year.
Attach the analytical review with explanations to the close pack for the reviewer.
checklist.done: an analytical review with written explanations for every material variance and key Medicare ratios is attached to the close pack.

checklist.step: Obtain independent statutory review of the populated blank
actions: Route the populated blank, mapping exception report, reconciliations, validation report and analytical review to a reviewer who prepared none of it.
The reviewer re-performs the GL-to-blank tie for the ten largest Medicare lines and initials each.
Log every review comment with a disposition and confirm the blank was re-validated after any change.
Record the reviewer name and sign-off date at least 10 business days before the filing deadline.
checklist.done: an independent reviewer has initialled the ten largest Medicare lines and signed off at least 10 business days before the deadline.

checklist.step: Prepare the jurat page and officer certifications
actions: Populate the jurat page with the entity name, NAIC company code, FEIN, statutory home office address, and the current officer and director list.
Confirm the officers named are those in office at the signature date against the board records.
Route for signature by the officers the blank requires and arrange notarisation where the state of domicile demands it.
File the executed jurat page with the close pack.
checklist.done: an executed, correctly officered jurat page is filed with the close pack, notarised where the domicile requires it.

checklist.step: Lock the blank and freeze the supporting pack
actions: Lock the statement in the reporting software so no page can change without a documented reopen.
Freeze the supporting pack: trial balance extract, mapping workbook, reconciliations, actuarial handover, validation report, analytical review and sign-offs.
Record the locked version number and the lock timestamp on the close checklist.
Where a reopen is unavoidable, require Chief Financial Officer approval, re-run all validations and re-obtain reviewer sign-off.
checklist.done: the statement is locked with a recorded version and timestamp, and any reopen carries CFO approval and a full re-validation.

checklist.step: Hand the locked statement to the filing team
actions: Transfer the locked statement file, the executed jurat page and the supporting pack to the Regulatory Reporting Manager who owns the NAIC and state filings.
Provide the filing team with the entity list, NAIC codes and the deadline for each filing (March 1 annual; May 15, August 15, November 15 quarterly).
Obtain a written receipt confirming the version handed over.
File the close pack in the financial reporting repository indexed by entity, statement year and period.
checklist.done: the filing team holds a receipted, locked statement version with the jurat and support, and the close pack is filed by entity and period.

testing.step: Build the population of Medicare blank lines subject to test
actions: Extract from the locked statement every line carrying a Medicare amount: Analysis of Operations Medicare column, Exhibit of Premiums Enrolment and Utilization, Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2, Schedule H Parts 1 to 3 and Schedule T.
Record for each line the reported amount, the prior-period amount and the entity NAIC code.
Add every line the NAIC validation suite flagged during the cycle, whether or not it was explained.
Sign the population stating the statement version and extraction timestamp.
testing.done: a signed population of Medicare-bearing blank lines exists, tied to a named locked statement version.

testing.step: Reconcile the blank back to the locked statutory trial balance
actions: Pull the locked trial balance using the timestamp recorded on the close checklist and re-run the mapping to blank lines yourself.
Compare your mapped totals to the reported blank amounts line by line; the difference must be nil.
Investigate any non-nil difference to the account and journal and state whether the mapping or the posting is wrong.
Confirm the trial balance used has the same extract timestamp the preparer recorded - a different extract is an exception.
testing.done: the blank reconciles to the locked trial balance with nil differences and a matching extract timestamp.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of lines and supporting records
actions: Take 100 percent of Medicare lines above the planning materiality threshold and 100 percent of lines that failed a validation check.
Take 10 further lines at random with a recorded seed from the remainder.
Within the premium and claims lines take 25 underlying transactions each, selected with the recorded seed.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and the selection date.
testing.done: a stratified, reproducible sample covers all material and failed lines plus a seeded selection of transactions.

testing.step: Re-perform the Medicare member-month and premium derivation
actions: Take the CMS Monthly Membership Reports for every month of the period and total member months by H-number yourself.
Total the CMS Monthly Payment Reports and derive capitation revenue, excluding Part D amounts.
Compare to the exhibit figures and compute the variance against the 0.1 percent member-month tolerance.
Trace every reconciling item claimed by the preparer (retroactive adjustments, risk adjustment true-up) to the CMS report line that supports it.
testing.done: member months and premium are independently recomputed from CMS reports and fall within the 0.1 percent tolerance.

testing.step: Re-perform the claims-to-ledger tie and the service-category split
actions: Extract paid Medicare claims by service category for the period directly from the claims platform using your own filters.
Compare category totals and the grand total to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2 and the utilization exhibit.
For 25 sampled claims open the claim in the platform and confirm the service category, paid amount and paid date used in the extract.
Confirm the claim is for a benefit the plan is required to cover under 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b) and is not a denied basic benefit misposted as an expense.
testing.done: claims totals and categories are independently reproduced and 25 claims are verified to the source with benefit coverage confirmed.

testing.step: Re-perform the Schedule T state allocation
actions: Take the county of residence from the CMS Monthly Membership Report and independently allocate premium to states.
Compare to the Schedule T amounts state by state and list every difference above the materiality threshold.
Cross-check the state list to the entity's certificates of authority and flag any premium allocated to an unlicensed state.
Confirm the Schedule T grand total equals reported premium on the Statement of Revenue and Expenses.
testing.done: Schedule T is independently reallocated, ties to reported premium and shows no premium in an unlicensed state.

testing.step: Test the actuarial reserve handover into the blank
actions: Take the Appointed Actuary's signed handover and trace each reserve figure to the ledger balance and the blank line.
Recompute Schedule H Part 3 development from the paid and reserve triangles and compare to the reported development.
Confirm the premium deficiency reserve test was performed and documented for the Medicare line.
Flag any reserve amount changed after the actuarial handover without a documented actuarial re-sign.
testing.done: every reserve in the blank traces to a signed actuarial handover with Schedule H development recomputed.

testing.step: Test the validation, review and lock controls
actions: Re-run the NAIC validation suite on the locked statement and compare the failure list to the filed validation report.
Confirm every explained failure has a written explanation naming the check number and the amount.
Confirm the reviewer sign-off date is at least 10 business days before the filing deadline and that the reviewer prepared none of the lines.
Read the software audit log for any change after the lock timestamp and confirm each carries CFO approval and a re-validation.
testing.done: the re-run validation matches the filed report, sign-off timing and segregation hold, and post-lock changes are CFO-approved.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with entity, NAIC code, blank line, amount misstated and the direction of the error.
Assign a coded root cause: mapping error, unmapped account defaulted, membership source stale, claims filter wrong, reserve changed post-handover, validation explained without support.
Set an owner and a remediation date; where a filed statement is misstated above materiality, open an amended-filing assessment with the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next statement cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, for material misstatement, an amended-filing assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds: nil GL-to-blank difference, zero unresolved validation failures, member months within 0.1 percent.
Confirm the signing reviewer prepared or posted none of the lines tested.
Report the conclusion, misstatements and any amended-filing decision to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer, and minute it.
File the signed workpaper with the trial balance extract, sample seed, CMS report copies and validation output in the financial reporting repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and minuted Audit Committee reporting is filed in the financial reporting repository.

checklist.step: Rebuild the filing obligation matrix from the licence register
actions: Pull the current certificate-of-authority register and list every state in which each MA-writing entity is licensed, with the licence effective and expiry dates.
Create one matrix row per entity per state per statement period, carrying the state's statutory due date and the accepted filing method.
Add the NAIC Financial Data Repository upload as its own row per entity per period.
Have the Controller confirm the entity list and Regulatory Counsel confirm the state list before the matrix is used.
checklist.done: a confirmed matrix exists with one row per entity per state per period plus the NAIC row, built from the licence register.

checklist.step: Confirm each state's current filing requirements
actions: Open each state insurance department's annual and quarterly statement filing checklist for the statement year and read the requirements for a health entity.

Record per state: electronic filing accepted through the NAIC Financial Data Repository only, or an additional state portal or hard copy required; whether an original signed jurat is demanded; and the filing fee amount and payment method.
Copy the exact due date sentence and its statutory cite onto the matrix row - do not carry the date forward from last year.
Save the dated checklist capture as <state>-filing-checklist-<statement year>.pdf against the matrix row.
checklist.done: every matrix row carries a quoted due date, a statutory cite, the accepted method, the fee and a dated checklist capture.

checklist.step: Confirm NAIC iSite+ filing access before the window
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and confirm the filing role for each NAIC company code the entity files under.
Confirm the backup filer holds the same role and that neither account has lapsed for inactivity.
Where access is missing, submit the NAIC access request naming the company code and role and record the request date and reference.
Record the confirmed access and its expiry against every NAIC matrix row.
checklist.done: an active primary and backup NAIC filer exists for every company code, evidenced by a dated access confirmation.

checklist.step: Generate the NAIC-format filing file from the locked statement
actions: Take the locked statement version receipted from the Controller and confirm the version number matches the receipt.
Run the software's electronic filing export to produce the NAIC-format file and the required bar-coded PDF pages.
Re-run the electronic filing validation on the exported file and confirm zero hard errors before transmitting anything.
Record the export file name, its checksum and the statement version it came from on the matrix row.
checklist.done: a validated NAIC-format export exists, checksummed and tied to the receipted locked statement version.

checklist.step: Upload the filing to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open the Financial Data Repository filing upload for the company code, statement year and period.
Attach the electronic filing file and the bar-coded PDF and submit, then wait for the repository to return the filing status.
Read the returned validation results and correct and re-upload immediately where the repository rejects the file - a rejected upload is not a filing.
Capture the confirmation screen showing company code, period, status and timestamp.
checklist.done: the NAIC upload returns an accepted status with a captured confirmation showing company code, period and timestamp.

checklist.step: Make the state-specific filings the matrix requires
actions: For each state whose checklist requires more than the NAIC repository filing, submit through the state's portal or send the hard copy to the address on the checklist.
Include everything the state demands: signed and notarised jurat, bar-coded pages, filing checklist certification and any state-specific supplement.
Use a tracked delivery method for hard copies and record the tracking number on the matrix row.
Capture the portal confirmation or the delivery proof against the row.
checklist.done: every state requiring a separate filing has a captured portal confirmation or tracked delivery proof on its matrix row.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fees and evidence the payment
actions: For each state with a fee, initiate payment by the method the checklist states (state portal card payment, EFT to the department account, or cheque with the filing).
Match the payment amount to the fee on the matrix row and reject any payment request without a matrix row behind it.
Record the payment reference, date and amount on the row and file the remittance advice.
Confirm cleared payment on the bank statement and flag any returned or unapplied payment to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst within 2 business days.
checklist.done: every fee is paid at the checklist amount with a payment reference on the row and clearance confirmed on the bank statement.

checklist.step: File the risk-based capital report with the annual statement
actions: Prepare the health RBC filing from the locked annual statement and confirm the total adjusted capital and authorised control level figures tie to the statement.
Upload the RBC filing to the NAIC by March 1 alongside the annual statement, and to the domiciliary state where it requires a separate copy.
Confirm the RBC ratio and record whether any company action level trigger is breached; notify the Chief Financial Officer immediately if it is.
Capture the RBC upload confirmation on its own matrix row.
checklist.done: the RBC filing ties to the annual statement, was uploaded by March 1 and its ratio and any trigger breach are recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing matrix to confirmations at each deadline
actions: On the statutory due date run the matrix filtered to rows without a captured confirmation and work each one before close of business.
For each open row establish whether the filing was made and the confirmation not captured, or the filing was not made at all.
Record the outcome on the row with the time it was resolved.
Report the completion status per entity to the Controller and the Chief Financial Officer on the due date.
checklist.done: on each due date every matrix row shows either a captured confirmation or a recorded, escalated non-filing.

checklist.step: Escalate any filing that will miss its statutory date
actions: Where a filing cannot be made on time, decide the course the same day: file with a known deficiency and amend, or file late with a notification to the state.
Have Regulatory Counsel draft and clear the notification to the state insurance department, stating the reason and the firm filing date.
Record the decision, the notification date and the recipient on the matrix row.
Assess and record the penalty exposure and whether the delay must be reported to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: every missed statutory date has a same-day decision, a counsel-cleared state notification and a recorded penalty assessment.

checklist.step: Handle state analyst enquiries arising from the filing
actions: Log every enquiry received from a state financial analyst or the NAIC with the receipt date and the stated response window.
Assign the response to the owner of the line questioned - Appointed Actuary for reserves, Statutory Reporting Manager for blank mechanics, Medicare finance lead for Part C figures.
Draft the response with the supporting schedule attached and have Regulatory Counsel review it before it leaves.
Send within the stated window and capture the transmission evidence against the filing row.
checklist.done: every analyst enquiry is logged, owned, counsel-reviewed and answered within the stated window with captured evidence.

checklist.step: File amended statements through the same controls
actions: Where a misstatement is identified after filing, prepare an amended statement from a new locked version rather than editing the filed one.
Obtain Chief Financial Officer approval of the amendment and a fresh independent reviewer sign-off on the changed lines.
Upload the amended filing to the NAIC repository flagged as an amendment and re-file with every state that received the original.
Capture the amended confirmations and cross-reference them to the original filing rows.
checklist.done: every amendment comes from a new locked version with CFO approval, is refiled to all original recipients and is cross-referenced.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing log to the NAIC record
actions: After each cycle pull the NAIC iSite+ filing history for every company code and compare it to the internal filing log.
Confirm the period, statement type and received date on the NAIC record match the log row.
Investigate any filing the NAIC record does not show, or shows with a different date, before the cycle is closed.
Sign the reconciliation and file it with the cycle pack.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows the internal filing log agreeing to the NAIC iSite+ filing history for every company code.

checklist.step: Debrief the cycle and update the matrix for next period
actions: Within 10 business days of the cycle close review every late row, rejected upload and missing confirmation with the owners.
Update the state filing matrix for any requirement, due date or fee change learned during the cycle.
Assign preventive actions with owners and dates and track them to closure.
Minute the debrief and circulate the updated matrix version.
checklist.done: a minuted debrief exists with owned preventive actions and a republished, updated filing matrix version.

checklist.step: Archive the filing evidence pack
actions: Bundle per entity per period: the filed statement version, NAIC upload confirmation, state receipts and delivery proofs, fee payment evidence, analyst correspondence and the NAIC reconciliation.
File under Statutory Filings > <entity> > <statement year> > <period> and apply the 10-year retention label.
Confirm retrieval by NAIC company code, state and period.
Record the archive reference on each filing log row.
checklist.done: the filing evidence pack is archived with a 10-year label and retrievable by NAIC company code, state and period.

testing.step: Rebuild the filing obligation population from the licence register
actions: Take the certificate-of-authority register directly and expand it to one obligation row per entity per state per statement period.
Add the NAIC Financial Data Repository row and the RBC row for the annual cycle.
Do not build from the filing matrix - the matrix is the control under test.
Sign the population stating the licence register version and extraction date.
testing.done: a signed obligation population is built independently from the licence register, including NAIC and RBC rows.

testing.step: Reconcile the independent obligations to the filing log
actions: Match each obligation to a filing log row on entity + state + period.
List obligations with no log row as potential unfiled statements and pursue each to a confirmation or an exception.
List log rows with no obligation and confirm the entity was genuinely licensed in that state for the period.
Present the reconciliation bridge with all differences resolved.
testing.done: every obligation matches a filing row or is raised as a potential unfiled statement, with a documented bridge.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100 percent of NAIC repository filings, 100 percent of RBC filings and 100 percent of domiciliary state filings.
Take 20 state rows at random with a recorded seed from the remaining non-domiciliary states.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and the selection date.
Add as mandatory rows any filing previously reported late or amended.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all NAIC, RBC and domiciliary filings plus a seeded selection of other states.

testing.step: Re-perform the due-date determination from the state source
actions: For each sampled state open the department's current filing checklist or statute and read the due date yourself before looking at the matrix row.
Compare your derived date to the recorded date; any difference is an exception, including a correct date with the wrong cite.
Confirm the accepted filing method recorded matches what the state's checklist says it accepts.
Capture the checklist page relied upon with its retrieval date into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independently derived due date and method compared to the matrix, with the source captured.

testing.step: Verify each filing directly in NAIC iSite+ and the state records
actions: Open the NAIC iSite+ filing history for each sampled company code and read the statement type, period and received date from the system.
For state portal filings open the portal receipt or the department acknowledgement rather than relying on the saved capture.
For hard-copy filings verify the tracked delivery record shows receipt at the department address on the checklist.
Flag any filing with no independently verifiable record as an exception regardless of internal assertions.
testing.done: every sampled filing is verified in the regulator's own record or an independent delivery record.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness against the statutory dates
actions: Compare each verified received date to the statutory date - March 1 annual, May 15, August 15 and November 15 quarterly, or the state variation.
Compute days early or late for every sampled row and list every late filing with the number of days.
Confirm the RBC filing date is on or before March 1 for every entity.
Confirm no filing relied on a mailing date where the state requires receipt by the due date.
testing.done: days early or late is computed for every sampled filing against the correct statutory or state-varied date.

testing.step: Test that what was filed is what was locked and reviewed
actions: Recompute the checksum of the archived filed export and compare it to the checksum recorded at generation.
Confirm the statement version behind the export is the version receipted from the Controller and signed off by the independent reviewer.
Open the filed bar-coded PDF and confirm the jurat page is executed by officers in office at the signature date.
Flag any filing made from an unreviewed or reopened version.
testing.done: every sampled filing traces to a checksummed, reviewer-signed locked version with a validly executed jurat.

testing.step: Test fee payment and analyst enquiry handling
actions: For each sampled state with a fee, compare the amount paid to the checklist fee and confirm clearance on the bank statement.
Flag any fee paid late, at the wrong amount, or returned and not re-paid.
Take every analyst enquiry logged in the period and recompute the response elapsed time against the state's stated window.
Confirm each response carries evidence of Regulatory Counsel review before transmission.
testing.done: fees agree to the checklists and cleared, and every analyst enquiry was answered in window with counsel review evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with entity, NAIC code, state, period, statutory date, actual date and the penalty exposure.
Assign a coded root cause: state omitted from matrix, due date carried forward, NAIC access lapsed, upload rejected and not re-sent, fee unpaid, confirmation not captured.
Set an owner and remediation date; for any late filing confirm a counsel-cleared state notification exists and open a penalty assessment.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, for late filings, a notification and penalty assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the zero-late, zero-unconfirmed threshold and compute the exception rate by entity and state.
Confirm the signing reviewer holds no NAIC iSite+ filing credentials and made none of the sampled filings.
Report late filings, unfiled states and penalty exposure to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer, and minute it.
File the signed workpaper with the licence-derived population, sample seed, regulator confirmations and timeliness recomputation under a 10-year label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and minuted Audit Committee reporting is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Derive the required supplemental list for each entity
actions: Take the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplemental filing list for the statement year and mark every item applicable to a health entity writing Medicare Advantage.
Add each domiciliary and non-domiciliary state's supplemental checklist items - state-specific exhibits, certifications and data calls.
Build the supplemental inventory with one row per entity per schedule showing the due date, the accepted format and the preparer.
Have the Controller confirm the inventory before preparation begins, and record any item deliberately marked not applicable with the reason.
checklist.done: a confirmed supplemental inventory exists per entity with due dates, preparers and a written reason against every not-applicable item.

checklist.step: Assign an owner, source and deadline to every schedule
actions: Name the preparer and the independent reviewer for each inventory row - Investment Operations for Schedule D, Legal for Schedule Y, Medicare finance for the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit.
Record the source of record per schedule: general ledger, investment accounting system, claims platform, CMS membership reports or the holding company register.
Back-schedule each row: source data due T-30, draft T-20, cross-checks clear T-10, sign-off T-5 from the schedule's due date.
Publish the schedule of milestones to all preparers and reviewers.
checklist.done: every inventory row has a named preparer, reviewer, source of record and four back-scheduled milestone dates.

checklist.step: Prepare the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit Medicare segment
actions: Populate the exhibit's Medicare column with earned premium, incurred claims, expenses for improving health care quality, cost containment and other administrative expense.
Allocate shared administrative expense to the Medicare segment on the documented driver (member months, claim counts or direct time), and record the driver and its values.
Confirm the Medicare column premium and claims agree to the Analysis of Operations Medicare column and to Schedule H Part 1.
Attach the allocation workbook showing the driver, the pool being allocated and the resulting Medicare share.
checklist.done: the Medicare column is complete, agrees to Schedule H and the Analysis of Operations, and carries a documented allocation workbook.

checklist.step: Reconcile the exhibit's member months and enrolment to CMS data
actions: Total member months from the CMS Monthly Membership Reports for the statement year by H-number and map them to the reporting entity.
Compare to the member months reported in the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit and to the Exhibit of Premiums, Enrolment and Utilization.
Explain every difference with a named cause - retroactive enrolment adjustments, mid-year contract novation, members outside the reporting entity.
Attach the reconciliation with the CMS report references to the exhibit workpaper.
checklist.done: exhibit member months reconcile to the CMS Monthly Membership Reports with every difference named and evidenced.

checklist.step: Prepare Schedule Y holding company and related-party disclosures
actions: Produce the Part 1 organisational chart from the corporate register showing every affiliate, its domicile, NAIC code and ownership percentage as at 31 December.
List in Part 2 every material transaction with affiliates in the year - management services agreements, tax sharing, intercompany reinsurance, cost allocations - with amounts.
Confirm each disclosed agreement is the version currently in force and, where the domiciliary state requires it, that a Form D non-disapproval was obtained.
Sign the schedule and hand it to the Statutory Reporting Manager with the supporting agreements referenced.
checklist.done: Schedule Y shows a current organisational chart and every material affiliate transaction with amounts and in-force agreement references.

checklist.step: Prepare the investment schedules and confirm valuations
actions: Extract the position-level holdings at 31 December with CUSIP, par, book adjusted carrying value, fair value and NAIC designation.
Confirm each NAIC designation against the NAIC Securities Valuation Office record and flag any security lacking a current designation.
Populate Schedule D Parts 1 and 2 and the Schedule DA short-term investments detail, and confirm totals tie to the Assets page.
Attach the custodian statement reconciliation showing par and market value agreement at 31 December.
checklist.done: investment schedules tie to the Assets page, every designation is confirmed and the custodian reconciliation is attached.

checklist.step: Prepare the Management's Discussion and Analysis
actions: Draft the discussion covering results of operations, liquidity and capital resources, and the material Medicare Advantage drivers - membership movement, risk score change, medical cost trend and CMS payment settlements.
Tie every figure quoted in the narrative to the filed annual statement page and line, and record the tie in the margin of the working draft.
Have the Appointed Actuary review the reserve and trend commentary and the Medicare Compliance Officer review any statement about program compliance.
Submit the approved discussion for filing by the April 1 deadline.
checklist.done: an approved discussion exists with every quoted figure tied to a statement page and line, reviewed by actuarial and compliance.

checklist.step: Prepare the risk-based capital supporting detail
actions: Populate the health RBC pages from the annual statement: underwriting risk by line including the Medicare business, asset risk from Schedule D designations, and credit risk.
Confirm the underwriting risk factor applied to the Medicare line matches the current NAIC RBC instructions.
Reconcile the total adjusted capital to capital and surplus on the Liabilities page plus the permitted adjustments, item by item.
Record the RBC ratio and, if any action level is approached, brief the Chief Financial Officer before filing.
checklist.done: RBC pages tie to the annual statement, use current-year factors and the total adjusted capital reconciliation is complete item by item.

checklist.step: Coordinate the actuarial opinion and supporting memorandum
actions: Issue the statement of actuarial opinion on the reserves as at 31 December for filing with the annual statement by March 1.
Prepare the supporting actuarial memorandum with the reserve methodology, data reconciliation to Schedule H and the reliance statements, for the domiciliary state's deadline.
Confirm the data relied upon reconciles to the claims and membership data underlying the Medicare segment of the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit.
Sign and date the opinion and file the memorandum with the confidentiality treatment the state allows.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial opinion is filed with the annual statement and the memorandum reconciles to the Medicare segment data.

checklist.step: Coordinate the audited financial report and internal control communication
actions: Agree the external audit timetable so the audited statutory financial report can be filed by June 1.
Provide the auditor with the filed annual statement, the supplemental schedules and the Medicare segment reconciliations.
Track every audit adjustment and decide whether it requires an amended annual statement or is recorded in the following period.
File the audited report and the management letter response with the domiciliary state by its deadline.
checklist.done: the audited statutory report is filed by June 1 with every audit adjustment assessed for an amended statement.

checklist.step: Run the cross-checks from each supplemental to the annual statement
actions: Run the software's supplemental cross-check suite and the NAIC supplemental validation for each schedule.
Tie the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit totals to the Statement of Revenue and Expenses, Schedule D totals to the Assets page and Schedule Y amounts to the related-party note.
Work every failure to nil difference or a written explanation naming the check and the amount.
Print the final validation output and file it with each schedule.
checklist.done: every supplemental cross-checks to the annual statement with nil difference or a documented explanation.

checklist.step: Obtain independent review of every supplemental
actions: Route each completed schedule with its source extract, allocation workbook and cross-check output to the assigned reviewer who prepared none of it.
The reviewer re-performs the allocation on the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit Medicare column and initials the workbook.
Log every review comment with a disposition and re-run cross-checks after any change.
Record the reviewer name and sign-off date at least 5 business days before the schedule's due date.
checklist.done: each supplemental carries a dated independent reviewer sign-off at least 5 business days before its due date.

checklist.step: File the supplementals to the NAIC and the states
actions: Upload the supplementals through NAIC iSite+ to the Financial Data Repository under the correct company code and statement year.
File the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit and the Management's Discussion and Analysis by April 1, and any schedule due with the annual statement by March 1.
Submit state-specific supplements through each state's required channel per the filing matrix.
Capture every confirmation and record its number and timestamp on the inventory row.
checklist.done: every supplemental is filed by its deadline with a captured confirmation recorded on the inventory row.

checklist.step: Close the inventory and confirm nothing was omitted
actions: Review the supplemental inventory after the June 1 date and confirm every row shows either a filed confirmation or a documented not-applicable reason.
Investigate every open row personally before the inventory is signed as complete.
Sign the completeness attestation naming the entity, statement year and any residual item with its remediation date.
Report completion to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: a signed completeness attestation exists per entity with every inventory row either filed or justified as not applicable.

checklist.step: Archive the supplemental evidence pack
actions: Bundle per entity per statement year: the supplemental inventory, each filed schedule, allocation workbooks, reconciliations, cross-check output, sign-offs and filing confirmations.
File under Statutory Filings > <entity> > <statement year> > Supplementals and apply the 10-year retention label.
Confirm retrieval by NAIC company code, schedule name and statement year.
Record the archive reference on each inventory row.
checklist.done: the supplemental evidence pack is archived with a 10-year label and retrievable by company code, schedule and year.

testing.step: Derive the required supplemental population independently
actions: Take the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplemental filing list for the statement year and mark every item applicable to a Medicare-writing health entity.
Add the domiciliary and non-domiciliary state supplemental checklists from each department's website.
Expand to one required row per entity per schedule; do not start from the internal inventory.
Sign the population stating the instruction edition and the state checklists relied on.
testing.done: a signed, independently derived population of required supplementals exists per entity.

testing.step: Reconcile the required population to the supplemental inventory
actions: Match each required row to an inventory row on entity + schedule + statement year.
List required rows with no inventory entry as potential omissions and pursue each to a filing confirmation or an exception.
For every item marked not applicable read the written reason and test it against the instruction's applicability criteria.
Present the reconciliation bridge with all differences resolved.
testing.done: every required supplemental matches an inventory row or is raised as an omission, with not-applicable reasons tested.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100 percent of the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit, Schedule Y, the RBC pages and the actuarial opinion for every entity.
Take 8 further schedules at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, across entities.
Within the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit take every allocation driver and 25 underlying expense postings.
Record the seed, strata, population sizes and the selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all key schedules per entity plus a seeded selection of the remainder.

testing.step: Re-perform the Medicare segment allocation in the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit
actions: Take the allocation pool and the stated driver values and recompute the Medicare share yourself.
Compare to the reported Medicare column and list every difference with its amount.
Test the driver for reasonableness - member months must come from the reconciled CMS figure, claim counts from the claims platform extract - and flag any driver with no independent source.
For 25 sampled expense postings trace to the ledger entry and confirm the cost centre supports the Medicare allocation applied.
testing.done: the Medicare allocation is independently recomputed, driver sources verified and 25 postings traced to the ledger.

testing.step: Cross-check each sampled schedule to the filed annual statement
actions: Tie the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit premium and claims to the Analysis of Operations Medicare column and Schedule H Part 1.
Tie Schedule D totals to the Assets page and Schedule DA to the short-term investment line.
Tie Schedule Y related-party amounts to the related-party note and to the intercompany balances in the Liabilities page.
List every non-nil difference with the amount and pursue it to the source before concluding.
testing.done: every sampled schedule cross-checks to the filed annual statement with all non-nil differences investigated.

testing.step: Re-perform the CMS membership reconciliation
actions: Total member months from the CMS Monthly Membership Reports for the statement year yourself, by H-number and entity.
Compare to the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit and the Exhibit of Premiums, Enrolment and Utilization figures.
Trace every reconciling item claimed by the preparer to the CMS report line or the enrolment adjustment that supports it.
Flag any unexplained difference regardless of size as an exception.
testing.done: member months are independently totalled from CMS reports and every reconciling item is traced to a supporting source.

testing.step: Test Schedule Y completeness against the corporate and contract registers
actions: Take the corporate register and the contract lifecycle management repository and list every affiliate and every in-force intercompany agreement at 31 December.
Compare to the Schedule Y Part 1 chart and Part 2 transaction list and flag every omission.
For each disclosed agreement confirm the amount disclosed agrees to the ledger intercompany account for the year.
Where the domiciliary state requires Form D approval, confirm the non-disapproval letter exists and pre-dates the transaction.
testing.done: Schedule Y is confirmed complete against the corporate and contract registers with amounts tied and Form D approvals verified.

testing.step: Test timeliness, review segregation and the actuarial opinion
actions: Compare each sampled supplemental's filing confirmation timestamp to its statutory date - March 1, April 1 or June 1 as applicable.
Confirm the reviewer sign-off pre-dates the filing by at least 5 business days and that the reviewer prepared none of the schedule.
Confirm the actuarial opinion is signed, dated and filed with the annual statement, and that the memorandum reconciles to Schedule H.
Flag any schedule filed without a completed sign-off or with a sign-off dated after the filing.
testing.done: filing timestamps, sign-off timing and segregation are verified, and the actuarial opinion and memorandum are confirmed filed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with entity, schedule, amount affected and the deadline missed or cross-check failed.
Assign a coded root cause: schedule omitted from inventory, allocation driver unsupported, membership source not reconciled, affiliate transaction undisclosed, sign-off after filing.
Set an owner and a remediation date; where a filed supplemental is misstated, open an amended-filing assessment with the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next statement year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and, for misstatements, an amended-filing assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds: zero supplementals omitted, nil cross-check differences, Medicare segment reconciled to Schedule H and CMS data.
Confirm the signing reviewer prepared none of the schedules tested.
Report omissions, misstatements and any amended-filing decision to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer, and minute it.
File the signed workpaper with the independently derived required list, sample seed, allocation re-performance and cross-check output under a 10-year label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and minuted Audit Committee reporting is filed in the financial reporting repository.
